commits.pr_title: [Model] Add native ShieldGemma 2 support for /classify
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Serve `google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it` natively through `/classify`. The response is one score, P(Yes) that the image violates the policy in the prompt. The model is `as_seq_cls_model(Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration)` plus a `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP` entry that selects `from_2_way_softmax` over the `No`/`Yes` tokens, following `d3.py`.

Not a duplicate: no open or merged PR adds ShieldGemma 2. #7084 and #15147 are about ShieldGemma 1 (text) and are closed.

## Claims

- `vllm serve google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it --runner pooling` loads the original checkpoint and answers `POST /classify` with `probs: [P(Yes)]`. No conversion script, no `hf_overrides`, no `--chat-template`.
- Scores match the Transformers `ShieldGemma2ForImageClassification` reference on public images: prompt lengths equal on 2100/2100 image/policy pairs, agreement at 0.5 of 100% on COCO (300 pairs) and 99.33% on the C4Censor sample (1800 pairs, 489 positive).
- ~70 lines of Python plus a 33-line chat template, reusing `as_seq_cls_model` and `load_weights_using_from_2_way_softmax`.

## Validation

Tests run on this branch (H100; vLLM nightly 7c3a9302f with this branch's Python files on top, base cbb38c458):

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_shieldgemma2.py      # 7 passed
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k ShieldGemma2        # 1 passed
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py                              # 459 passed, 2 skipped (not ShieldGemma2)
```

Parity setup. Reference: `ShieldGemma2ForImageClassification` + `ShieldGemma2Processor`, bf16, separate process, same GPU. vLLM: this PR's files on top of upstream main 7c3a9302f, transformers 5.23.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, NVIDIA H100 NVL, `--runner pooling --max-model-len 8192`, original JPEG sent as a data URL. Policies: the 3 defaults of `ShieldGemma2Processor` (`dangerous`, `sexual`, `violence`).

| set | pairs | ref. positives | agreement @0.5 | mean \|ΔP(Yes)\| | max \|ΔP(Yes)\| | prompt length equal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| COCO val2017, 100 random images | 300 | 3 | 100% | 4.1e-4 | 0.037 | 300/300 |
| C4Censor sample, 600 images | 1800 | 489 | 99.33% | 6.1e-3 | 0.549 | 1800/1800 |

- COCO: 100 images drawn with `random.Random(1)` over the sorted val2017 ids. COCO is benign, so agreement says little there; the |ΔP| and length columns are the informative ones.
- C4Censor: the public preview sample (4 categories × 3 subcategories × 50 images), Dutta et al., J. Comput. Soc. Sci. 9:34 (2026), <https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.30946031> (figshare license field: CC BY 4.0). Files checked by SHA-256 against the public archive (600/600 match). Not redistributed.
- Prompt lengths equal the reference's `attention_mask` length on every pair (409 / 414 / 419 per policy), i.e. vLLM sees the same two `<bos>`.
- Max |ΔP| on C4Censor: one image carries EXIF orientation 8. vLLM applies `exif_transpose` on load; the reference's `Image.open().convert("RGB")` does not. With the reference on the rotated image the total becomes 99.39%, mean 5.8e-3, max 0.46. Details below.
- Run-to-run: two server starts with default batching differ by up to 1.3e-2 (mean 1.8e-4) over the 2100 pairs, and 1 decision flips at 0.5 (batch-dependent kernels). At `--max-num-seqs 1` two starts agree to 7.3e-9, and the hand-written classifier from alternative 3 below matches this PR to 4.5e-7, with 0 differing decisions.

### How to reproduce

The model is gated: accept the license on the Hub and set `HF_TOKEN`.

```shell
vllm serve google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it --runner pooling --max-model-len 8192
```

```shell
curl -s http://localhost:8000/classify -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "model": "google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it",
    "messages": [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/image.jpg"}},
                {"type": "text", "text": "No Violence/Gore content: the image shall not contain content that depicts shocking, sensational, or gratuitous violence."}
            ]
        }
    ]
}'
```

Image before the policy text, one policy per request. `data[0].probs[0]` is P(Yes).

Parity script: `parity_public.py`, in the first comment of this PR. It downloads the COCO images itself; for C4Censor pass the extracted figshare archive with `--c4censor-dir`.

```shell
python parity_public.py select    ./data
python parity_public.py reference ./data
vllm serve google/shieldgemma-2-4b-it --runner pooling --max-model-len 8192 &
python parity_public.py vllm      ./data http://localhost:8000
python parity_public.py compare   ./data http://localhost:8000
```

## Details

<details>
<summary>Design and alternatives</summary>

### The two-way softmax is exact

The reference computes `softmax(logits[:, -1, [yes, no]])`. Without a final logit softcap, `softmax([a, b])[0] = sigmoid(a - b) = sigmoid((e_Yes - e_No) · h)`, with `e` the `lm_head` rows. `from_2_way_softmax` builds that one-row head from `lm_head[Yes] - lm_head[No]` in fp32 (`vllm/model_executor/models/adapters.py:592-594`). With a softcap the identity breaks (`tanh` is not linear), so `ShieldGemma2ForImageClassificationConfig` raises `ValueError` if `final_logit_softcapping` is set; the checkpoint loads, so it is not.

The head has one output row, so the classify pooler applies a sigmoid (`vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/seqwise/poolers.py:133`). The `No`/`Yes` ids come from the tokenizer (3771 / 10784, the reference's defaults). The config entry is needed because with `convert none` `SequenceClassificationConfig` does not run (`vllm/config/vllm.py:2981-2985`).

### Alternatives considered

1. `--convert classify` on the original checkpoint:
   - (a) The name does not resolve: `_normalize_arch` tries `ShieldGemma2ForCausalLM` / `ForConditionalGeneration`, which are not registered (`vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:1430-1454`).
   - (b) Overriding `architectures` to Gemma 3 fails: `Gemma3ProcessingInfo.get_hf_config` type-checks the config class (`vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py:262`), and `hf_overrides` changes attributes, not the class.
   - (c) Gemma 3's mapper (`gemma3_mm.py:516-523`) maps `model.language_model.` to `language_model.model.`; this checkpoint nests one level deeper and ends up as `language_model.model.model.*`.
2. Aliasing the architecture to Gemma 3 in the registry: hits (b) and (c) and changes Gemma 3 for everyone.
3. A hand-written classifier with its own head and pooler. I wrote that first. At `--max-num-seqs 1` it gives the same decisions as this adapter form and a bit-identical `score.weight`, with more code, so the adapter form won.

### Processor

`ShieldGemma2Processor` ignores `text`, builds one prompt per (image, policy) from its own template and calls `Gemma3Processor`. Here the client sends one policy per request, so vLLM uses `Gemma3Processor` (`gemma3_mm.py:85-86`); `ShieldGemma2ProcessingInfo` only changes the expected config class. Prompt lengths match on all 2100 pairs.

### Prefix-LM mask

Gemma 3 sets `is_mm_prefix_lm` on `text_config` (`gemma3_mm.py:566`), but the arch-config convertor reads `hf_config` and otherwise falls back to a model-type list (`vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py:357-370`). `"shieldgemma2"` is added to that list. On an internal set, removing the entry dropped agreement from 0.985 to 0.945.

### Chat template and `<bos>`

The reference prompt starts with two `<bos>`: the Hub template writes one and Transformers' tokenizer adds another (`add_special_tokens=True`). vLLM's chat path does not add BOS by default, so this PR adds `shieldgemma2` to `_MODEL_TYPES_OVERRIDING_TOKENIZER_CHAT_TEMPLATE` (`vllm/transformers_utils/chat_templates/registry.py:50`) with `template_shieldgemma2.jinja` (Hub template plus one leading `<bos>`), and widens that function's docstring to cover this case. A test asserts the rendered `ours == "<bos>" + hub`.

Alternative: no override, and clients send `add_special_tokens: true` (`vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/protocol.py:297-298`). That gives the reference tokens too, but the default (`false`) then drops one `<bos>` and the score changes without any error. Measured on one COCO image: without the override the prompt is one token shorter on each policy (413 / 408 / 418) and P(Yes) changes by 1.5–2× (all scores near 0 for that image, so no decision changes). The two do not combine: override plus `add_special_tokens: true` gives three `<bos>`.

### Other changes

- `"shieldgemma2"` in `_FLOAT16_NOT_SUPPORTED_MODELS` (`vllm/config/model.py:2536`), like `gemma3`.
- Docs: `classify.md` (supported models).
- `tests/models/registry.py`: in `_SEQUENCE_CLASSIFICATION_EXAMPLE_MODELS`, next to D3 and LlamaNemotronVL. `test_common.py` only iterates `_MULTIMODAL_EXAMPLE_MODELS`, so those two are not covered there either. Happy to add a processing test for sequence-classification VLMs in a follow-up.
- The `/classify` smoke test needs a 24 GB GPU and `HF_TOKEN` with license access, like other gated examples.

### Limitations

- Tensor parallel untested. The loader indexes the local shard of the embedding, as for the existing `from_2_way_softmax` models.
- Float16 rejected; use bf16 or fp32.
- One policy per request.

</details>

<details>
<summary>C4Censor tail</summary>

The 30 pairs with the largest |ΔP| (28 images) were rerun: vLLM at `--max-num-seqs 1` twice, the reference twice in separate processes.

| comparison (30 pairs) | mean \|ΔP\| | max \|ΔP\| |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM batch 1, run 1 vs run 2 | 2.5e-4 | 7.5e-3 |
| vLLM batch 1, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, run 1 vs run 2 | 0 | 0 |
| reference, run 1 vs run 2 | 0.049 | 0.258 |
| vLLM batch 1 vs reference | 0.137 | 0.549 |

- vLLM's own run-to-run difference at batch 1 comes from prefix caching: the three policies of an image share the image prefix, and whether a request hits the cache depends on arrival order. With prefix caching off, two runs are bit-identical; vLLM vs reference does not change (mean 0.137, max 0.549). The effect is intermittent: the 2100-pair run above gave 7.3e-9.
- `pixel_values` as computed by the reference and by vLLM are identical for 27 of the 28 images and for 28 control images with |ΔP| < 0.01. The exception is the EXIF image, which is the 0.549 pair; the reference on vLLM's pixels moves it from 0.44 to 0.98 (vLLM: 0.99).
- On these near-boundary pairs the reference disagrees with itself by mean 0.049; vLLM at batch 1 differs from it by mean 0.137. About a third of the gap is reference nondeterminism; the rest is consistent with different bf16 kernels near the boundary. Computing the reference head in fp32 instead of bf16 moves it by at most 0.056. We did not isolate it further. On the control pairs all of these are below 0.01.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Stream Muse tool-call arguments
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust Muse unified parser buffers each ATEM block until `</atem:function_calls>`, so a tool call produces no deltas until the whole block has been generated. This PR streams Muse tool-call arguments as they are generated, using the `OpenToolCall` writer already used by the JSON-style, DSML and Kimi K3 parsers (#66528, #66529, #66530).

## Claims

- Each `<atem:invoke>` streams as its own tool call. The name goes out once the invoke open tag is complete, and the call closes at `</atem:invoke>` rather than at the end of the block.
- A parameter whose schema admits only `string` streams as escaped JSON string fragments as it arrives. Its value is the raw text, unchanged, including text that looks like ATEM tags other than `</atem:parameter>` and `</atem:invoke>`.
- Any other parameter is written once its value is complete, decoded by the existing `convert_parameter_value`. The resulting JSON is the same as before.
- A last parameter missing its `</atem:parameter>` ends right before `</atem:invoke>`, dropping one separating newline, as proposed in #64270. Before, the value streamed through the rest of the turn and the unfinished call was dropped at the end.
- Non-streaming output comes from the same parser state, so non-streaming responses are unchanged.

## Validation

Unit tests (`rust/`, base `2d4457d333`):

```text
cargo test -p vllm-parser muse   -> 40 passed
cargo test -p vllm-parser --lib  -> all passed
cargo test -p vllm-chat          -> all passed except grammar_replay, which fails here only on Hugging Face downloads (PermissionError) and has no Muse cases
cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy -p vllm-parser --all-targets -- -D warnings -> clean
```

New or changed tests:

- `muse_tool_call_streams_before_close_tag`: the name and argument fragments are emitted before `</atem:invoke>`.
- `muse_streaming_tool_calls_match_batch_for_every_marker_split`: for every split point of a multi-parameter call, the merged streamed deltas equal the one-shot parse.
- `muse_string_parameter_keeps_atem_tags_in_its_value`
- `muse_unclosed_last_parameter_*` (4 tests from #64270) and `muse_unclosed_last_parameter_streams_and_keeps_later_segments`: a value missing `</atem:parameter>` ends at `</atem:invoke>`, streamed and buffered, and later segments stay visible.
- `muse_repeated_parameter_keeps_first_value`
- `muse_atem_block_without_invoke_fails`
- Existing streaming-vs-batch comparisons now compare merged per-call deltas, since one call can now span several deltas. The `muse_mixed_channels_match_python_routing` snapshot content is unchanged.

End to end with a real checkpoint: `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4` on 4x B300, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve ... --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser muse --reasoning-parser muse --enable-auto-tool-choice`, with a single `shell` tool (`command: string`, `timeout: integer`).

<details>
<summary>Streamed tool-call deltas (stream=true)</summary>

```text
"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_29e4230e9d404878bd8b0db5","type":"function","function":{"name":"shell"}}]}
"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":0,"function":{"arguments":"{\"command\": \""}}]}
"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":0,"function":{"arguments":"# This for loop prints numbers 1 to 20, each on its own line\\nfor i"}}]}
"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":0,"function":{"arguments":" in {1..20}; do echo \\\"$i\\\"; done"}}]}
"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":0,"function":{"arguments":"\""}}]}
"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"index":0,"function":{"arguments":"}"}}]}
"finish_reason":"tool_calls"
```

Before this change the same request emits the name and the full arguments in one delta after `</atem:function_calls>`. The concatenated arguments are valid JSON. The same request with `stream=false` returns the complete call with `finish_reason: tool_calls`.

</details>

## Details

Behavior changes beyond chunking:

- **Repeated parameter:** a parameter repeated within one invoke keeps its first value, because that value may already be on the wire. Before, and in the Python parser, the last value wins. Kimi K3 (#66530) makes the same choice. The model's chat template does not produce repeated parameters.
- **Malformed block:** calls that completed before the malformation stay emitted. Before, the whole block failed together. The parser still fails on the malformation, and the serving layer falls back to plain text from that point, as before.
- **Truncated output:** output that ends inside an invoke (e.g. `max_tokens`) leaves that call's streamed name and partial arguments on the wire. The unfinished markup is still dropped. This matches the other streaming parsers.

The Python Muse tool parser still emits a call only when its invoke closes. This PR changes only the Rust parser's chunking. The merged content of the tool calls matches Python.

Overlap with open PRs: #64270 (last parameter missing its close tag), #64568 (nullable string parameters) and #67972 (doubled tool names) also touch `rust/src/parser/src/unified/muse.rs`. Whichever lands second needs a rebase. This PR includes #64270's Rust rule and tests, so #64270 is left with the Python parser and docs. #67972's `normalize_tool_name` is called unchanged in `InvokeOpen`. No open PR streams Muse tool-call arguments in the Rust frontend.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Report engine errors on completion streams that request logprobs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Since #62872 the Rust frontend answers an engine `validation_error` with 400 and a retryable engine error with 503. A `/v1/completions` stream that requests `logprobs` still hides both. When the engine finishes the request with an error, the stream looks for generated logprobs first and sends `completion stream requested logprobs but generation returned none` as an internal server error in place of the engine's error. Since #64220 an echoed stream reads its prompt logprobs when it starts, so with or without generation it sends `echoed completion prompt requested logprobs but generation returned none` instead.

This PR checks the terminal finish reason before it asks for logprobs, so the stream reports the engine's error. An echoed stream holds a missing prompt logprobs error until the request finishes, reports the engine's error when there is one, and still fails as before when the request finishes normally without prompt logprobs.

It also stops the engine client from logging a validation error at error level as an engine failure, as it already does for retryable errors, and drops "internal" from the `FinishReason::Error` doc, since the error can now be the client's.

An earlier version of this PR added the 400 mapping itself, which #62872 has since landed, so this version keeps only the stream fix. It also turned an untyped engine error on non streaming `/inference/v1/generate` into a 500; #62872 keeps that as finish reason `error`, like Python, and this version leaves it so.

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

```
cd rust
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy -p vllm-server -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-llm --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --no-fail-fast -p vllm-server -p vllm-llm -p vllm-engine-core-client
```

`engine_request_errors_map_to_http_status` gains three completion streams that request logprobs, a plain one, an echoed one and a prompt only one, so both the retryable and the validation error run through them. `completion_chunk_stream_rejects_missing_prompt_logprobs` covers a prompt only stream that finishes normally without prompt logprobs.

## Test Result

| Completion stream with `logprobs` that the engine ends with an error | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain stream | `InternalServerError`: `completion stream requested logprobs but generation returned none` | the engine's error: 503 for a retryable one, 400 for a validation error, with its message |
| echoed stream, with or without generation | `InternalServerError`: `echoed completion prompt requested logprobs but generation returned none` | the engine's error, as above |

On main with only the new test cases, the route test fails on the first of them:

```
/v1/completions {"model":"Qwen/Qwen1.5-0.5B-Chat","prompt":"hello","logprobs":1,"stream":true}: data: {"error":{"message":"completion stream requested logprobs but generation returned none","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}
```

With the change, `cargo test` over the three crates passes 743 of 743, and `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Prefer tokenizer.json over tekken.json
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a model ships both `tekken.json` and `tokenizer.json`, the Rust frontend loads `tekken.json` (`tokenizer_file()` in `rust/src/text/src/backend/hf/model_files.rs`). That order dates from a pre-tokenizer regex bug in older Mistral `tokenizer.json` files, and it now causes two problems:

- `mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B` does not load: its `tekken.json` carries `model_settings_builder.reasoning_effort: "low"` and other new builder fields, which the `tekken` crate (0.2.0, the latest release) rejects with `unknown variant 'low', expected 'none' or 'high'`.
- The `tekken` crate encodes text without matching control tokens. The Rust frontend renders Mistral chat through the model's HF chat template, so on a repo whose `tekken.json` does load, a rendered `[INST]`, `[AVAILABLE_TOOLS]` or `[THINK]` reaches the model as plain text. Current Mistral `tokenizer.json` files list every control token as an added special token.

This PR loads `tokenizer.json` first and keeps `tekken.json` as the fallback for repos that ship no `tokenizer.json`.

## Claims

- Mistral Large 4 loads and its chat render matches `mistral_common`: `/v1/chat/completions/render` of a user message with one tool returns 74 token IDs, equal to `mistral_common` 1.13.1 `encode_chat_completion` on the same request, with control tokens as special IDs.
- Repos that ship both files and use v3/v13/v15 tokenizers (Nemo-2407, Ministral-8B-2410, Ministral 3, Large 3, Devstral 2, Small 4, Medium 3.5, Large 4) now encode chat control tokens as special tokens.
- Repos with only one of the two files keep their tokenizer.
- `resolve_tokenizer_source` loses its `tekken_path` parameter, which every caller passed as `None`.

## Validation

Rust CI set on the head of this branch (`fb0644d4d4`, on `92b9817e02`):

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2846 passed, 13 skipped
```

- New test `resolved_model_files_prefer_tokenizer_json_over_tekken`: a directory with both files resolves to `tokenizer.json`, a Tekken-only directory to `tekken.json`. With the old order it fails with `expected HuggingFace tokenizer, got Some(Tekken(...))`.
- On the same change based on `f7f17bcfe8`, `mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B` from the Hub (fresh `HF_HUB_CACHE`, config and tokenizer files only): `vllm-rs render` starts, where `main` exits with the `tekken` parse error, and the render above matches `mistral_common` on all 74 IDs.
- On the same `f7f17bcfe8` base, `mistralai/Magistral-Small-2509` (Tekken only) still loads through Tekken (`loading tokenizer with Mistral Tekken`).

## Details

**Which repos change.** About 40 `mistralai` instruct/chat repos were surveyed: tokenizer files grouped by hash, and 7,505 strings fuzzed against `mistral_common` 1.13.1.

| Group | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| No `tekken.json` (Mistral-7B v0.1–v0.3, Mixtral, Codestral-22B, Large-2407/2411, Small-2409) | `tokenizer.json` | unchanged |
| Tekken only (Pixtral-12B-2409, Devstral-Small-2505/2507, Magistral-Small-2506/2507/2509, Small-3.2-2506, Voxtral, Large-3-2512-BF16, Leanstral) | `tekken.json` | unchanged |
| Both files, v3/v13/v15 (Nemo-2407, Ministral-8B-2410, Ministral 3, Large 3, Devstral 2, Small 4, Medium 3.5, Large 4) | `tekken.json` (Large 4 fails to load) | `tokenizer.json`: same regex as `tekken.json`, 0 mismatches in the fuzz |
| Both files, v7 (Small-24B-2501, Small-3.1-2503) | `tekken.json` | `tokenizer.json`, which keeps the old Llama-3-style split: 4.3% of adversarial fuzz strings differ; on real text 0–0.18% of tokens differ and the text decodes identically |

**Accepted differences, with no code to compensate:**

- The v7 `tokenizer.json` split above: no regex check or Tekken fallback for those two repos.
- `/v1/completions` BOS on v13/v15 repos. Their `tokenizer.json` has no BOS post-processor and `tokenizer_config.json` sets no `add_bos_token`, while Tekken adds BOS. A text prompt there loses its leading `<s>` (`"Hello"` goes from `[1, 22177]` to `[22177]` on Ministral 3), and `prompt: ""` tokenizes to no tokens and returns 400 instead of a BOS-only prompt. Chat is unaffected, since the chat template renders `<s>` itself.

**Comparison with Python.** Python `--tokenizer-mode auto` uses `mistral_common` for a Mistral repo that ships `tekken.json` (`resolve_tokenizer_args` in `vllm/tokenizers/registry.py`). The Rust frontend renders through the HF chat template rather than `mistral_common`'s request encoder, and for the v3/v13/v15 repos `tokenizer.json` produces the same IDs, so its behavior here equals Python `--tokenizer-mode hf`.

**Layering.** Model-file resolution owns the choice of tokenizer file (`vllm-text`, `tokenizer_file()`). Nothing downstream reads which file was picked other than the tokenizer constructor, and no parser depends on Tekken: the Mistral reasoning and tool parsers match control tokens that both tokenizers expose as special tokens.

**Not a duplicate.** A search of open and closed PRs for `tekken`, `tekken.json` and `tokenizer.json` found no PR that changes the order. vllm-project/vllm#67663 (closed unmerged) took the other route, making the HF renderer emit control-token IDs when the tokenizer is Tekken; with `tokenizer.json` preferred, that path remains only for Tekken-only repos. vllm-project/vllm#64768 (fill files missing from a cached Hub snapshot) and vllm-project/vllm#64162 (vocab/merges-only repos) touch the same file for unrelated cases.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept --enable-offline-docs, --aggregate-engine-logging and --uvicorn-log-level as no-ops
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`--enable-offline-docs`, `--aggregate-engine-logging` and `--uvicorn-log-level` fail Rust frontend startup as unsupported arguments, on both `vllm-rs serve` and the Python-supervised `--args-json` path, although none of them has anything to do in the Rust frontend. This PR accepts each as a no-op with the usual warning, one commit per flag.

## Claims

- `--enable-offline-docs`: Python serves `/docs` and `/redoc` from vendored assets instead of a CDN (`vllm/entrypoints/launchers/app.py`, `serve/instrumentator/offline_docs.py`). The Rust frontend serves no FastAPI docs endpoints, and `--disable-fastapi-docs` is already a no-op for the same reason.
- `--aggregate-engine-logging`: Python logs one aggregated periodic stats line across data-parallel engines instead of one per engine (`AsyncLLM` → `vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`). The Rust periodic stats line (`rust/src/llm/src/log_stats.rs`) always aggregates across engines, so the flag asks for what Rust already does. Without the flag the frontends still differ in log format (Python per engine, Rust aggregated).
- `--uvicorn-log-level`: the Rust frontend runs no uvicorn; its log level comes from `--log-level` / `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL`.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), based on `92fd8cc668`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2762 passed, 13 skipped
```

Each commit on its own also passes fmt, workspace clippy and the workspace nextest.

`noop_args_are_accepted` now covers the three flags on both paths; with the `Unsupported` markers restored it fails at startup parsing. The three tests that used `uvicorn_log_level` as their example of an unsupported argument (`serve_args_reject_unsupported_flag_arg`, `frontend_args_json_rejects_unsupported_fields`, `frontend_args_json_aggregates_multiple_unsupported_fields`) now use `--tool-server`, which stays a startup error.

## Details

Each flag moves from `Unsupported` to `Noop` in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/unsupported.rs`, the CLI layer that owns startup-argument compatibility: hidden from help, and warning "currently has no effect in Rust frontend, ignoring". `--enable-offline-docs` sits next to `--disable-fastapi-docs`. `--aggregate-engine-logging` sits in `EngineUnsupportedArgs`, so under `vllm-rs serve` the `Noop` consumes it and the managed engine does not receive it; that is harmless because only the Python frontend (`AsyncLLM` and its stat loggers) reads it.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes these three flags in the Rust frontend; vllm-project/vllm#48138 edits the neighboring `--disable-uvicorn-access-log` declaration only.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Treat an undefined value's length as 0 in chat templates
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Jinja2's `length` filter (and its `count` alias) is Python's `len`, and Jinja2's default `Undefined` has length 0; chat templates rely on that to guard optional variables. MiniJinja's `length` errors on an undefined value, so the Rust frontend returns a 500 where Python renders. This PR makes the HF renderer's `length`/`count` return 0 for an undefined value.

## Claims

- A chat request without tools on `examples/tool_chat_template_hermes.jinja` renders under the Rust frontend instead of failing with HTTP 500 `cannot calculate length of value of type undefined (in chat:37)`. The template guards with `{%- if tools is iterable and tools | length > 0 %}`, and the Rust renderer leaves an absent `tools` undefined; an undefined value is iterable in both Jinja2 and MiniJinja, so evaluation reaches `length`.
- The same holds for templates that apply `length` directly to an optional message key, such as `message['tool_calls']|length` on an assistant message without tool calls (the Rust renderer omits the key).
- `none | length` still errors, as `len(None)` does in Jinja2.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), based on `92fd8cc668`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2763 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `test_length_of_undefined_is_zero` renders the Hermes guard plus `missing | count` and `[1, 2] | length` (`none 0 2`) and snapshots the `none | length` error. With the two `add_filter` lines removed it fails with `cannot calculate length of value of type undefined`, the production error.
- Python reference (transformers' `ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment`, Jinja2 3.1.6): `{{ x is iterable }} {{ x|length }} {{ x|count }}` with `x` undefined renders `True 0 0`; `{{ x|length }}` with `x=None` raises `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`.
- `vllm-rs render NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_hermes.jinja`: `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` with one user message, with and without `"tools": []`, renders; a `vllm-rs` from `main` returns the `length of value of type undefined` error for both. The 184 rendered token IDs equal transformers' `apply_chat_template` with the same template and `add_generation_prompt=True`.
- E2E on a GB200 node with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and a release `vllm-rs` from this change: `pytest -v -s tool_use/test_chat_completions.py --models hermes -k "test_chat_completion_without_tools or test_chat_completion_with_empty_tools"` gives 2 passed; on `main` both fail with the HTTP 500 above. The Rust frontend CI lane runs `tool_use` with `--models=llama3.2` only, so these Hermes cases are not in CI today.

## Details

The filter is registered in the HF renderer's template environment (`build_environment` in `rust/src/chat/src/renderer/hf/template.rs`), which already carries the other Jinja2/transformers compatibility shims (the `pycompat` method callback, `tojson`, `strftime_now`, `raise_exception`). It returns 0 for an undefined value and otherwise delegates to `minijinja::filters::length`. This is Jinja2 semantics rather than a per-template or per-model fix, so it applies to every HF chat template, server-configured or request-supplied.

On the Python side, the frontend passes `tools=None` to transformers, so `None is iterable` is false and the Hermes guard short-circuits; but even an undefined `tools` renders under Jinja2, where `Undefined.__len__` is 0.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes the Rust chat template filters.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] List valid model aliases when a model is not found
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a request's `model` names neither a served base model nor a loaded LoRA adapter, the Python frontend answers 404 `NotFoundError` with `param: "model"` and ``The model `X` does not exist. Valid aliases: <served base names, comma-separated>.`` (`OpenAIServing._check_model`, vllm-project/vllm#59889), and since vllm-project/vllm#67765 it bounds the echoed name to 256 characters plus `...`. The Rust frontend returned only ``The model `X` does not exist.`` with the name echoed unbounded, and reused that model error for unloading an adapter that is not loaded. This PR gives the Rust frontend Python's message, alias list and bound, and its own 404 for the unload case.

## Claims

- An unknown model on every HTTP route that checks the model (chat, completions, Responses, generate, tokenize/detokenize, and the render server's routes) returns Python's 404 error object: the message lists the served base names as aliases (loaded LoRA adapters are not listed, like Python), `param: "model"`.
- The echoed model name is cut to its first 256 characters plus `...` past 256 characters, counted in characters as Python counts code points; lookup still uses the full name.
- `/v1/unload_lora_adapter` for an adapter that is not loaded returns a 404 `NotFoundError` about the adapter (``LoRA adapter `X` is not loaded``) with `param: null`, like Python's `_check_unload_lora_adapter_request`, instead of the model-not-found error. The wording stays the Rust LoRA routes' own.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), on `dfe50bce9a` based on `92b9817e02`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2847 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `routes::tests::load_lora_adapter_registers_model_and_forwards_lora_request`: with `adapter-a` loaded, an unknown model returns the full Python error object listing only the base name; unloading the adapter a second time returns the adapter 404 with `param: null`.
- `routes::tests::generative_scoring_rejects_invalid_requests_before_submission`: its unknown-model case now shows the alias list.
- `model_names::tests::unknown_model_lists_base_names_only`, and `error::tests::model_not_found_bounds_echoed_model_name` (256 characters kept whole, 257 cut, counted in characters), plus the error-class and error-log snapshots.
- With the alias list built from base plus adapter names and unload mapped back to the model error, `unknown_model_lists_base_names_only` and the LoRA route test fail.
- Python tests that pin this behavior: `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py::test_inference_invalid_model_error_is_bounded` (its `batch-chat` case targets `/v1/chat/completions/batch`, which the Rust frontend does not serve), `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_launch_render.py::test_render_invalid_model_error_is_bounded`, and `tests/entrypoints/serve/lora/test_serving_models.py::test_unload_lora_adapter_not_found`.

## Details

- **Layering.** `ServedModelNames::check` is the consumer of the requested model name and owns the set of selectable names, so it is the one place that knows which of them are base names. `ServedModelNames` now keeps served base names apart from loaded adapter names (`with_names` becomes `with_adapter_names`, `names()` becomes `base_names()`; every caller of each already held base names only). A request may still select either kind; on a miss, `check` builds `ApiError::ModelNotFound { model, served_names }` with the base names only. The message and the echo bound are rendered in `ApiError::to_error_response` with the other wire messages.
- **LoRA unload.** Unload's not-found is a LoRA registry error, so `UnloadLoraError::NotFound` maps to the existing `ApiError::NotFound` in `routes/lora.rs`, next to the other LoRA error mappings.
- **gRPC** keeps its own `NOT_FOUND` status text.
- **Why base names only.** Python lists the served base names as aliases; `/v1/models` makes the same split between base cards and adapter cards.

**Not a duplicate.** A search of open PRs for the alias message, model-not-found errors in the Rust frontend, and Rust LoRA unload found none on this path; vllm-project/vllm#67138 registers `--lora-modules` names on the Python render server and touches no Rust code.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Unload a LoRA adapter an engine already evicted
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On the Rust frontend, unloading a LoRA adapter that an engine's LRU cache has already evicted answers 500, and the adapter can then never be unloaded and stays in `/v1/models`. This PR treats the engine's "not present" answer as success, which is the state unload wants. It is the unload half of vllm-project/vllm#60222 by i-m-aditya; credit to the author for finding it.

## Claims

- `POST /v1/unload_lora_adapter` (and the gRPC control unload) succeeds when an engine reports the adapter as already absent, and the adapter disappears from `/v1/models`.
- A failure to reach the engines, an engine-reported error, or a decoding error still fails the unload and keeps the registration.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), on `cb46fa5288` based on `92b9817e02`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2846 passed, 13 skipped
```

- New route test `unload_lora_adapter_succeeds_when_engine_already_evicted_it` scripts the engine to answer `remove_lora` with `false` and checks that the unload answers 200 and that `/v1/models` no longer lists the adapter. Without the fix it fails with `left: 500, right: 200`.

## Details

- **Engine.** The engine-side adapter state is a cache. Every generate request carries the adapter's full `LoRARequest`, path included, and a worker loads a missing adapter on demand (`vllm/lora/worker_manager.py`, `_apply_adapters` → `add_adapter`). Loading more adapters than `--max-cpu-loras` LRU-evicts the oldest. `remove_adapter` returns `False` only when the id is not cached (`vllm/lora/model_manager.py`).
- **Python.** `OpenAIServingModels.unload_lora_adapter` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/models/serving.py`) deletes the registration and answers 200 without calling the engine.
- **Rust before.** `LoraManager::unload_lora` calls `EngineCoreClient::remove_lora`, which ANDs every engine's result. When any engine answers `false`, Rust returned `UnloadLoraError::NotRemoved` (HTTP 500, gRPC `INTERNAL`) and kept the registration. With DP, a single engine that evicted the adapter was enough.
- **Change.** Rust still removes the adapter from the engines on unload, which frees their cache slots, but ignores a `false` result. `UnloadLoraError::NotRemoved` and its HTTP and gRPC mappings are removed (`rust/src/server/src/lora.rs`, `routes/lora.rs`, `grpc/control.rs`).
- **Scope.** vllm-project/vllm#60222 also cleans up after a failed load; that half is not included. The frontend registration is the commit point, so a partially failed fresh load leaves only engine cache entries under a never-reused id, which the LRU evicts. In review of #60222 on 2026-10-12 the maintainers approved the unload half and asked for the PR to be narrowed to it; the author has not responded since 2026-10-23, and the branch now conflicts with `main`.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for LoRA unload / `remove_lora` / `NotRemoved`: vllm-project/vllm#60222 is the inactive PR this supersedes (unload part only); vllm-project/vllm#54939 is the Python-side counterpart (making the Python frontend remove the adapter from the engine on unload, treating `False` as not an error), which this PR does not touch; vllm-project/vllm#54833 and vllm-project/vllm#51433 change LoRA load events and metrics, not unload.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Forward --seed to the spec_bench and speed_bench datasets
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`vllm bench serve` ignores `--seed` for `--dataset-name spec_bench` and `speed_bench`. Both loaders are built without `random_seed`, so their load-time shuffle always uses `BenchmarkDataset.DEFAULT_SEED`. This passes `args.seed`, as the other `get_samples()` loaders that shuffle or sample already do (#40788 made the same fix for `custom`).

## Claims

- `--seed` now selects which SPEC-Bench and SPEED-Bench prompts are sampled, and in what order.
- The default (`--seed 0`) sends exactly the same prompts as before.
- Every other `get_samples()` loader that shuffles or samples already honors `--seed`, and so does the Rust `vllm-bench` (see Details).
- `--seed` now has help text, so the `vllm bench serve` CLI reference says what it controls.

## Validation

Tested at 81280f431 (this branch, on main 898a7c68c). macOS arm64, CPU only: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.22.2, vLLM run from the source tree with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`.

The new tests fail with main's `datasets.py` and pass with this change:

```
$ VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py -q --tb=short --show-capture=no
# main's vllm/benchmarks/datasets/datasets.py, this PR's test file
_______ test_bench_dataset_seed_propagates[spec_bench-_write_spec_bench] _______
tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py:134: in test_bench_dataset_seed_propagates
    assert prompts_a != prompts_b
E   AssertionError: assert {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...} != {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...}
E     
E     Both sets are equal
______ test_bench_dataset_seed_propagates[speed_bench-_write_speed_bench] ______
tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py:134: in test_bench_dataset_seed_propagates
    assert prompts_a != prompts_b
E   AssertionError: assert {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...} != {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...}
E     
E     Both sets are equal
___ test_bench_serve_seed_changes_prompts_sent[spec_bench-_write_spec_bench] ___
tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py:178: in test_bench_serve_seed_changes_prompts_sent
    assert prompts_a != prompts_b
E   AssertionError: assert {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...} != {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...}
E     
E     Both sets are equal
__ test_bench_serve_seed_changes_prompts_sent[speed_bench-_write_speed_bench] __
tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py:178: in test_bench_serve_seed_changes_prompts_sent
    assert prompts_a != prompts_b
E   AssertionError: assert {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...} != {'row 0: uniq...prompt.', ...}
E     
E     Both sets are equal
FAILED tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py::test_bench_dataset_seed_propagates[spec_bench-_write_spec_bench]
FAILED tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py::test_bench_dataset_seed_propagates[speed_bench-_write_speed_bench]
FAILED tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py::test_bench_serve_seed_changes_prompts_sent[spec_bench-_write_spec_bench]
FAILED tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py::test_bench_serve_seed_changes_prompts_sent[speed_bench-_write_speed_bench]
4 failed, 3 passed, 10 warnings in 3.03s

# this PR
7 passed, 10 warnings in 2.89s
```

The other dataset tests that go through `get_samples()` still pass:

```
$ VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py \
    tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_chat_template_kwargs.py \
    tests/benchmarks/test_custom_image_dataset.py tests/benchmarks/test_random_dataset.py \
    tests/benchmarks/test_txt_slices_dataset.py tests/benchmarks/test_bfcl_dataset.py -q
42 passed, 42 warnings in 7.75s
```

By hand, with SPEC-Bench's real `question.jsonl`: the bench serve entry point (`vllm.benchmarks.serve.main`, which `vllm bench serve` runs) against a stub OpenAI completions server that logs each prompt it receives, with `--dataset-name spec_bench --skip-chat-template --num-prompts 5 --max-concurrency 1`. Prompts are listed as their row in `question.jsonl`:

```
# main
--seed 0 sent question.jsonl rows (category):
  136 (translation), 213 (summarization), 100 (translation), 142 (translation), 394 (math_reasoning)
--seed 1 sent question.jsonl rows (category):
  136 (translation), 213 (summarization), 100 (translation), 142 (translation), 394 (math_reasoning)

# this PR
--seed 0 sent question.jsonl rows (category):
  136 (translation), 213 (summarization), 100 (translation), 142 (translation), 394 (math_reasoning)
--seed 1 sent question.jsonl rows (category):
  459 (rag), 67 (stem), 192 (summarization), 47 (coding), 279 (qa)
```

## Details

- Root cause: in `get_samples()`, the `dataset_mapping` entries for `spec_bench` and `speed_bench` construct `SpecBench(...)` and `SpeedBench(...)` without `random_seed`, so `BenchmarkDataset.__init__` keeps `DEFAULT_SEED` (0) and `load_data()` runs `random.seed(0)` before `random.shuffle(self.data)` whatever `--seed` is. v0.34.0 has the same code.
- Impact: a run with `--seed N` measures the same prompts as `--seed 0`. Seed sweeps and "different seed" re-runs repeat prompts, and on a server with prefix caching or suffix decoding's cross-request corpus, the repeat hits caches the earlier run filled. `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` suggests varying `--seed` when cache reuse is not intended; for these two datasets that had no effect.
- Audit of the rest of `get_samples()`: `custom`, `custom_image`, `custom_audio`, `hf`, `sharegpt`, `burstgpt`, `random`, `random-mm`, `random-rerank` and `prefix_repetition` already pass `random_seed=args.seed`. `timed_trace` does not shuffle; it replays the trace in file order. `vllm bench throughput` shares `get_samples()` but doesn't offer these two datasets. In the Rust `vllm-bench`, `speed_bench` already passes `config.seed`, and the `spec_bench` flags are on its Python-only list (no Rust loader).
- Compatibility: `--seed` defaults to 0, which equals `DEFAULT_SEED`, so recipes and scripts that don't set `--seed` get the same prompts as before. Only runs with a non-zero `--seed` change, which is the fix.
- Docs: `--seed` had no help text; it now reads "Random seed for dataset sampling and shuffling." in the generated `vllm bench serve` CLI reference. The SPEC-Bench and SPEED-Bench examples in `docs/benchmarking/cli.md` don't pass `--seed`, so they select the same prompts as before.
- Tests: two, each parametrized over both loaders, in the existing `tests/benchmarks/test_custom_dataset_seed.py`. `test_bench_dataset_seed_propagates` parses the arguments with the real `add_dataset_parser()` and calls `get_samples()`. `test_bench_serve_seed_changes_prompts_sent` runs `vllm bench serve`'s parser (`add_cli_args()`) and `main_async()` against an in-process aiohttp stub of `/v1/completions`, and checks that `--seed 0` and `--seed 42` send different prompts. It uses a stub rather than `RemoteOpenAIServer` because only the prompts the client sends matter, and a real server would need a GPU and a model. The Benchmarks CLI CI step (`pytest -v -s benchmarks/`) runs both.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Keep response_format in chat /tokenize
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend's chat `/tokenize` request type has no `response_format` field, so serde silently drops it and `into_chat_request` hard-codes `response_format: None`. Renderers that put format instructions into the prompt (Kimi K3) therefore tokenize a different prompt than chat completions generate from, and an invalid `response_format` returns 200 where the Python frontend returns 400. This PR accepts `response_format` with the existing `ResponseFormat` type and passes it to the chat options, as the chat-completions path does.

## Claims

- With Kimi K3, `json_object` and `json_schema` instructions now appear in the tokenized prompt; `null` keeps the plain prompt. The rendered strings match Python's Kimi K3 renderer exactly.
- An invalid `response_format` (unknown type, incomplete `json_schema`) returns 400, matching Python. Valid requests on models that ignore the field are unchanged.

## Validation

Rust 1.95, aarch64 (DGX Spark), `main` at 29c6cfc457 (the touched files are unchanged on current `main`).

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-server tokenize_response_format_reaches_kimi_k3_prompt
cargo test -p vllm-server tokenize_rejects_invalid_response_format
cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
```

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tokenize_response_format_reaches_kimi_k3_prompt` (snapshot of the rendered Kimi K3 prompt for object / schema / null) | fails: all three prompts lack the format instructions | passes |
| `tokenize_rejects_invalid_response_format` (router entry point) | fails: 200 instead of 400 | passes |
| workspace tests | 2,730 passed, 3 failed, 14 ignored | 2,732 passed, same 3 failed, 14 ignored |

The 3 failures are pre-existing `vllm-chat` roundtrip snapshots (`roundtrip_mimo_v26`, `roundtrip_step5`, `roundtrip_kimi_k25`) and fail identically on `main`. Clippy, fmt and pre-commit pass.

Live check against a served `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, Python frontend vs the source-built Rust frontend, `POST /tokenize` with `"response_format": {"type": "not-a-format"}`: `main` gives Python 400 / Rust 200; with this PR both 400. Valid `json_object` and `null` requests give 200 and identical tokens on both.

## Details

`response_format` is boxed in `TokenizeChatRequest` so the untagged request enum does not grow enough to trip clippy's `large_enum_variant`. It is serialized into `ChatOptions.response_format`, the same value chat completions pass to the renderer. Tokenization still performs no generation or constrained decoding. Previously ignored malformed input now gets a 400, as in Python; serde and Pydantic error wording still differ.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs/issues for `rust tokenize`, `tokenize response_format`, `Kimi tokenize` and the tokenize source path (2026-11-17). #50543 wires Kimi formats in the Python Responses API; #62321 is about tokenize error mapping for unsupported messages; #67616 is LoRA tokenization. None adds the field to Rust `/tokenize`.

AI assistance was used for the investigation, implementation, tests, and review of this PR. The human submitter authorized its submission.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Reject a missing completions prompt with Python's message
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend declares the completions `prompt` field as required, so a request without `prompt` (or with `prompt: null`) fails JSON deserialization with serde's `missing field \`prompt\`` and `param: null`. Python rejects it with `"Either prompt or prompt_embeds must be provided and non-empty."` and `param: "prompt"`, which `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py::test_empty_prompt` pins. This PR gives the Rust frontend Python's check and message.

## Claims

- A completions request (`/v1/completions` and `/v1/completions/render`) with a missing or `null` `prompt` and no `prompt_embeds` gets Python's 400 message with `param: "prompt"`.
- `prompt_embeds: []` counts as absent, as in Python's `validate_prompt_and_prompt_embeds`: `prompt: "hi", prompt_embeds: []` is accepted, and `prompt_embeds is not supported.` fires only for actual embeddings, which stay unsupported.
- `test_empty_prompt` passes against the Rust frontend without relaxing it.

| Request | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|
| no `prompt` | 400 prompt message | 400 serde "missing field `prompt`" | 400 prompt message |
| `prompt: null` | 400 prompt message | 400 serde untagged-enum error | 400 prompt message |
| `prompt: null, prompt_embeds: []` | 400 prompt message | 400 serde error | 400 prompt message |
| no `prompt`, non-empty `prompt_embeds` | embeddings path | 400 serde "missing field `prompt`" | 400 `prompt_embeds is not supported.` |
| `prompt: "hi", prompt_embeds: []` | accepted | 400 `prompt_embeds is not supported.` | accepted |
| `prompt: ""` | 400 prompt message | tokenized (unchanged) | tokenized (unchanged) |

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`), based on `898a7c68c2`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2846 passed, 1 failed (see below), 13 skipped
```

- The one failure, `vllm-chat::roundtrip roundtrip_kimi_k25` (`stop token 163586 of "<|im_end|>" is not in the stop set {163585}`), comes from the node's shared Hugging Face cache: its snapshot of the latest `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` revision lacks `generation_config.json`. The test passes with an empty cache, and this PR does not touch `vllm-chat`.
- New route tests: `completions_reject_missing_prompt` (scripted mock engine) snapshots the four rejected `/v1/completions` requests above; `completions_render_checks_prompt_presence` pins the same missing-prompt 400 on the render route, `""` → `[BOS]`, `""` without special tokens → the empty-token 400, and `prompt` with `prompt_embeds: []` → accepted. With the production change reverted, both fail.
- E2E on a GB200 node with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and a release `vllm-rs` from this change (before the rebase onto vllm-project/vllm#68390): `pytest -v -s entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py -k "not prompt_embeds"` gives 2 passed (`test_empty_prompt` unrelaxed, `test_out_of_vocab_token_ids`); on `main`, `test_empty_prompt` fails with the serde message. The commented-out `test_prompt_validation.py` command in `.buildkite/test_areas/rust_frontend.yaml` can be enabled once this lands.

## Details

- **Layering.** `CompletionRequest.prompt` becomes `Option<CompletionPrompt>` on the wire. `prepare_completion_request`, shared by both completions routes, rejects `None` (a `let ... else`) before splitting the prompt into the per-prompt `TextRequest`s, so the check sits where the optional wire field becomes the required internal one. The `prompt_embeds` placeholder stays in `validate_request_compat`. The message names `prompt_embeds`, so it is completions-wire specific and nothing moves into `vllm-text`.
- **`prompt: ""` stays valid when the tokenizer adds BOS.** Python rejects the raw empty string before tokenizing, but the problem that check guarded against (vllm-project/vllm#7746) was an empty *encoded* prompt, and Python's own DTO accepts `[""]`. The Rust frontend leaves `""` to tokenization: with a BOS-adding tokenizer it is a valid document-start prompt (render returns `[BOS]`), and without one it fails as an empty token prompt (`token_ids must contain at least one token ID.`). This keeps current Rust behavior and is pinned by `completions_render_checks_prompt_presence`.
- **OpenAI.** The OpenAI reference defaults an omitted prompt to `<|endoftext|>`; vLLM rejects it instead, and this PR keeps that policy while giving the error Python's diagnostics.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#68098 also aligns the completions prompt check, but rejects `prompt: ""` as Python does, which this PR deliberately does not (see above). vllm-project/vllm#68390 (batched prompts, merged) changed the same `prompt` field; this PR is based on it, and a batch prompt keeps its behavior.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Check min_tokens against max_completion_tokens when both limits are set
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend rejects chat requests that set `min_tokens`, a `max_tokens` below it, and a larger `max_completion_tokens`, even though `max_completion_tokens` overrides `max_tokens` and the Python frontend accepts them. This PR checks `min_tokens` only against the limit that is actually used.

## Claims

- `{"min_tokens": 2, "max_tokens": 1, "max_completion_tokens": 8}` on `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions/render` now returns 200 with `min_tokens=2, max_tokens=8`, as on the Python frontend. On main it returns 400 `min_tokens cannot be greater than max_tokens`.
- `min_tokens` above the effective limit is still rejected, both when only `max_tokens` is set and when `max_completion_tokens` is.

## Validation

macOS arm64, Cargo 1.95, main `5d35ce393`. CPU only; no model weights needed.

- New unit test `validate_checks_min_tokens_against_the_effective_max_tokens` (six combinations of the three fields): fails on main on the `(2, 1, 8)` case, passes with this PR.
- HTTP check through the in-process router with the scripted engine used by `routes/tests.rs`: render, non-streaming chat and streaming chat with the request above. On main all return 400. With this PR they return 200, and the engine receives `min_tokens=2, max_tokens=8`. I ran these route tests locally and left them out of the PR, since the unit test covers the changed check.
- `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib routes::openai::chat_completions::`: 87 passed. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --tests` are clean.

```sh
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-server --lib routes::openai::chat_completions::
```

## Details

`ChatCompletionRequest::normalize` moves `max_tokens` into `max_completion_tokens` only when the latter is unset, so with both set the deprecated `max_tokens` is kept but never used as the output limit. `validate_chat_cross_parameters` still compared `min_tokens` with it. Python resolves the limit with `max_completion_tokens` taking precedence whenever it is not `None` (`ChatCompletionRequest.build_tok_params`). It checks `min_tokens` only against that resolved value (`SamplingParams._verify_args`), so the stale `max_tokens` has no effect there. The fix skips the `max_tokens` check when `max_completion_tokens` is set, using the same `is not None` precedence.

Not covered: completions has no `max_completion_tokens` field, so it is not affected.

```
Summary [   0.104s] 2 tests run: 1 passed, 1 failed, 703 skipped
# this branch

PASS [   0.087s] (2/2) vllm-server routes::tests::chat_structured_outputs_use_configured_backend
Summary [   0.101s] 2 tests run: 2 passed, 703 skipped
```

Python test on the CPU engine (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH` set to a `vllm-rs` built from the base, then from this branch; then the Python frontend):

```
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=5 pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_completion_with_function_calling.py::test_strict_tool_without_parameters
# Rust frontend built from the base
E               openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - Invalid structured outputs: [15:24:18] /project/cpp/grammar_compiler.cc:1318: Check failed: (std::holds_alternative<Grammar>(result)) is false: Invalid structural tag error: JSON schema format must have a json_schema field with a object or boolean value
======================== 1 failed in 178.01s (0:02:58) =========================
# Rust frontend built from this branch
======================== 1 passed in 186.71s (0:03:06) =========================
# Python frontend (VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0)
======================== 1 passed in 120.40s (0:02:00) =========================
```

Style and regressions, with CI's commands:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check          # exit 0
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # exit 0
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-bench --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
Summary [ 201.237s] 2244 tests run: 2244 passed (3 slow), 12 skipped
```

Mutation check: with `parameters: None` for every tool, the existing `absent_strict_is_non_strict` and `parameter_level_pins_argument_schemas` fail. With an empty object schema in place of `true`, the route test fails.
</details>

No model evaluation: the change only affects requests that failed before.

## Details

- **Root cause.** An omitted `parameters` is stored as `Value::Null` (`#[serde(default)]` in `routes/openai/utils/types.rs`; gRPC does the same for an empty `parameters_json`). `tool_params` passed it on as `Some(Null)`. The xgrammar structural-tag crate maps `None` to `true`, but uses `Some(Null)` as the schema of a strict tool. A non-strict tool gets `true` before the schema is read, which hid the bug. The Rust frontend does not compile the grammar, so the engine's xgrammar rejects it, and the frontend maps that validation error to 400.
- **Python.** It dumps the tool with `exclude_none=True` (`vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py`), and xgrammar maps a missing schema to `true`.
- **Design.** `Tool.parameters` stays a `Value`, so chat templates still see `"parameters": null`, like Python's. Making it `Option<Value>` is the larger alternative. I can do that instead if you prefer.
- **Other paths.** The line is shared by every crate grammar builder and by Kimi K3, so those are fixed too. Beam and HY read the schema their own way and do not change. `/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions/render` and gRPC `RenderChat` reach the same code; only chat completions is tested here.
- **Related, not a duplicate.** #50989 and its open fix #61147 are about strict tools whose schema is an empty object, which loop on Qwen models. #61147 changes the Python function I cite above, but keeps a missing schema as `true`. No issue or open PR covers this bug. The search covered `InvalidStructuralTagError`, `json_schema null`, `strict tool without parameters` and `tool-strict-level parameter`, and checked the open PRs that touch `output_grammar.rs`.
- **Docs.** None: no new flag, field or default.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code) to find the bug, to write the change and the tests, and to run the commands above on my laptop. I reviewed every changed line, and I ran the Rust route test before and after the fix.

commits.pr_title: [Core][Mamba] Remove mamba_cache_mode
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes `mamba_cache_mode`. Since the `"all"` mode was removed (#58997, #60043), it can only be `"align"` (prefix caching on) or `"none"` (off), so Mamba code now reads `cache_config.enable_prefix_caching` directly. The `--mamba-cache-mode` flag was already a deprecated no-op scheduled for removal in v0.34.0 (#64838); it is removed here too.

## Behavior changes

`"align"` was set once, by `MambaModelConfig` in `try_verify_and_update_config`, so it also meant "this model has Mamba layers" and stayed set if prefix caching was turned off later.

- Every replaced check is in Mamba-only code (Mamba layers, their metadata builders, `MambaManager`, `MambaHybridModelState`) or guarded by `has_mamba_layers`, a `MambaSpec` or `is_hybrid`, so it still applies to Mamba models only. The one model-agnostic check, chunked MM input in `VllmConfig`, is now guarded by `is_hybrid`.
- Two places still turn prefix caching off after that point: batch invariance on TRITON_MLA (at `Attention`/`MLAAttention` init) and MLA on a CPU without AMX. Hybrid models used to keep the `"align"` layout there with caching off; they now raise and ask for `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, since switching the layout that late would leave `mamba_block_size` at the attention block size.

commits.pr_title: [Core][EPD] Fail metadata-only items no EC or KV transfer covers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fail a request whose metadata-only multimodal item neither the EC connector nor a KV transfer covers, instead of scheduling a local encode with no pixels and killing the engine core. Part of #66093, **priority 2 of 4**. Independent: based on `main`, reproducible over HTTP today, and does not need #66094.

| Priority | PR | Scope | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #66094 | Proto + Rust gRPC/chat handoff + engine-role gate | — |
| **2 (this)** | #66928 | Scheduler backstop for metadata-only items. Shared by HTTP and gRPC | — |
| 3 | #66929 | `--allowed-local-media-path` / `--allowed-media-domains` on the Rust frontend | — |
| 4 | #66930 | Receiver cache: a metadata-only item must not replace the cached pixels. HTTP follow-up; a gRPC e2e does not hit it | #66928 |

This PR previously carried the engine-role gate; that gate is now part of #66094, since it fixes a review comment there.

## What happens today

An EC consumer or a multimodal KV consumer (`MultiModalConfig.allow_missing_mm_embeddings`) accepts multimodal items that carry only placeholder metadata, such as an HTTP `image_embeds` part holding just `image_grid_thw`. That is how HTTP EPD hands an image to PD without resending the pixels. The embedding is expected from the EC connector, or the prompt from the KV that P transferred. When neither covers the item, the scheduler treats it like any other encoder input and schedules a local encode. The model gets no pixels, `embed_multimodal` returns `None`, and the engine core dies on an assertion. One request takes the whole server down for every client.

It happens whenever the EC store no longer has the item (eviction, an encoder that wrote to a different store, or a client or router that sends metadata for something never encoded), and on a D that recomputes after a failed KV load.

Reproduced on `main` over HTTP with the Python frontend, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, one server:

| Server | Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| EC consumer (`ECExampleConnector`, empty store) | metadata-only `image_embeds` | 500, `EngineDeadError`, `/health` down, next request refused | 500 for this request; `/health` 200; next raw-image request 200 |
| KV consumer (`NixlConnector`), no KV transferred | same | 500, `EngineDeadError`, server down | 500 for this request; server keeps serving |

Root cause on `main`, from the engine log:

```text
AssertionError: Expected multimodal embeddings to be a list/tuple of 2D tensors, or a single 3D tensor, but got <class 'NoneType'> instead.
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

## What this PR does

`_reject_on_missing_encoder_input` runs where the scheduler would schedule a local encode, after the EC-hit path. If the engine accepts missing embeddings and the item has nothing the encoder can run on, it fails that request through the existing `encoder_cache_mismatch_reqs` path (`FINISHED_ERROR`) and logs why. `has_encoder_input` moves to `PlaceholderMetadataResolver` so the scheduler and `ECCPUScheduler` share one definition. Items with pixels, EC hits and KV-covered prompts are unaffected.

## Where the lines go

**+132 / −7** in 4 files (~54 code, ~78 tests).

| File | Code | Tests | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` | +38 | — | `_reject_on_missing_encoder_input` (~28): skip unless the engine accepts metadata-only items; if the item has nothing to encode, add the request to `encoder_cache_mismatch_reqs` and log why. One call where a local encode would be scheduled (~6), import + lazily built resolver (~4) |
| `ec_connector/utils.py` | +15 | — | `PlaceholderMetadataResolver.has_encoder_input`: does the item carry anything beyond placeholder metadata? |
| `ec_connector/cpu/scheduler/__init__.py` | +1 / −7 | — | `ECCPUScheduler` had its own copy of that check; it now calls the shared one |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` | — | +78 | EC miss with and without a KV connector; KV consumer with nothing transferred |

## How this helps Rust gRPC EPD and media handling

#66094 lets metadata-only items reach the engine over gRPC as well, for E+PD and E→P→D. This backstop sits in the shared worker path, so the same missed item fails one request instead of the engine, whichever frontend sent it. For a gRPC EPD router such as [vllm-project/router#553](https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/553), a stale EC handle becomes a request error it can retry with raw media, not a dead backend.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "metadata_only or ec_connector" -q
# 39 passed
```

New tests: `test_ec_connector_cache_miss_fails_metadata_only_item[False|True]` (EC miss, with and without a KV connector) and `test_kv_consumer_without_kv_fails_metadata_only_item` (KV consumer, no EC connector, nothing transferred). With `scheduler.py` reverted to `main`, all three fail: `assert '0' not in {'0': 200}`, meaning the item was scheduled for a no-input encode.

The HTTP reproduction above was run on unchanged `main` and on this branch.

Pre-commit against `origin/main`: passed.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: serve 6-8 decode rows with the HIP skinny GEMM on gfx1151
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

W4A16 decode on gfx1151 uses the HIP skinny GEMM only up to 5 rows; 6 or more rows fall to the Triton kernel, which is 1.7-4.6x slower on the layer shapes measured. 

This PR serves 6-8 rows with the HIP kernel. Serving Qwen3.8-27B, median TPOT drops 27% at 8 concurrent requests and 23% at 5, with GSM8K unchanged.

## Claims

- 6, 7 and 8 decode rows run 1.7-4.6x faster than the Triton fallback on gfx1151 (production dispatch, bf16, cache-flushed).
- 9 rows and more are unchanged (still Triton). Other targets keep the 5-row limit.
- Serving Qwen3.8-27B (Quark W4A16): median TPOT 131 -> 95 ms (-27%) at 8 concurrent requests and 122 -> 94 ms (-23%) at 5; 1 and 4 are unchanged. GSM8K accuracy is unchanged.

## Validation

Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), full CMake build of this branch for gfx1151, torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0.

**End to end.** `vllm serve` of Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16 (default compile and CUDA graphs, `--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32`). Both arms run the same build; "before" sets `MAX_SKINNY_BATCH_SIZE_GFX1151` back to 5, which is `main`'s dispatch.

```bash
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 \
  --ignore-eos --num-prompts $((4 * C)) --max-concurrency $C
```


| concurrency C | median TPOT before | after | output tok/s before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 74.7 ms | 74.4 ms (-0.4%) | 12.7 | 12.7 (+0.2%) |
| 4 | 81.6 ms | 81.5 ms (-0.1%) | 40.0 | 40.0 (-0.1%) |
| 5 | 121.7 ms | 93.6 ms (-23.0%) | 34.1 | 44.4 (+30.4%) |
| 8 | 131.2 ms | 95.5 ms (-27.2%) | 44.0 | 54.4 (+23.7%) |

5 requests gain as much as 8 because the default capture sizes are 1, 2, 4, 8, ..., so a batch of 5 runs in the size-8 graph, which this PR moves from Triton to HIP. One run per arm.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, first 400 test questions, chat with thinking off, temperature 0, concurrency 8: 386/400 (96.5%) before, 389/400 (97.25%) after; 393 of 400 answers are identical and none that was correct before is wrong after.

**Tests.** `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`: **436 passed** (bf16 and fp16). On the #63364 head alone, `test_hip_skinny_wvSplitK_int4_g` gave 116 passed on the same machine, which also covers the gfx11/gfx12 runtime check that PR lists as open. AMD CI runs this file on MI300 and MI355 only, where it skips (gfx11/gfx12 only), so these paths have no CI coverage; the runs above are the validation.

**Kernel.** Time per call through `_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply_impl`, bf16, cache-flushed. "Before" is the Triton fallback that 6-8 rows used on `main`:

| shape (K -> N) | rows | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8 gate_up 5120 -> 34816 | 6 / 7 / 8 | 818 / 810 / 815 us | 430 / 480 / 457 us | 1.90x / 1.69x / 1.78x |
| Qwen3.8 down 17408 -> 5120 | 6 / 7 / 8 | 514 / 511 / 517 us | 229 / 237 / 235 us | 2.24x / 2.15x / 2.20x |
| Qwen3.8 gdn_in_proj 5120 -> 16384 | 6 / 7 / 8 | 500 / 503 / 504 us | 206 / 231 / 222 us | 2.43x / 2.18x / 2.27x |
| Qwen3-8B qkv 4096 -> 6144 | 6 / 7 / 8 | 309 / 307 / 309 us | 68 / 69 / 70 us | 4.57x / 4.47x / 4.38x |
| Qwen3-4B qkv 2560 -> 3840 | 6 / 7 / 8 | 59 / 60 / 59 us | 31 / 32 / 32 us | 1.92x / 1.89x / 1.83x |

The Triton baseline on the K=4096 shape runs at only 42 GB/s; I did not look into why, so treat that row's ratio with care.

## Details

**Why 5.** The cap was inherited from the unquantized `wvSplitK` family, where N=5 was added for speculative decoding (#40687). The int4 kernel itself is not limited to 5: on gfx115x it walks K in LDS-sized chunks, so it runs for any `K * N`.

**Changes.**
- `skinny_gemms_int4_n6.cu` / `_n7.cu` / `_n8.cu`, plus their declarations, `case 6/7/8` and CMake entries, following #63364's per-`N_in` layout.
- `skinny_gemms_int4.cuh`: 6-8 rows take one tile, YTILE=4 / UNRL=1, chunked over K when the activation does not fit LDS. Off gfx1151 the host rejects these widths and their kernels compile to empty bodies (343 KB instead of 833 KB per unit on gfx1100).
- `rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`: `MAX_SKINNY_BATCH_SIZE_GFX1151 = 8`, gfx1151 only.

**Tile and cap.** Over 15 layer shapes at 6-8 rows, `(4, 1)` was within 7% of the best of five `(YTILE, UNRL)` tiles on 14 shapes, and HIP beat Triton in every cell. Past 8 rows the HIP kernel is level with Triton (about 110 GB/s at 16 rows), so the cap stays at 8. Max VGPR 190 / 210 / 228 for N = 6 / 7 / 8, no scratch.

**Not a duplicate.** No open or merged PR or issue in vllm-project/vllm or ROCm/vllm (searched 2026-11-05) raises the 5-row limit. Related: #63364 (dependency), #65322, #63562, #65754.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Kiro) was used for the investigation, the code and this description.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Use a uv-managed Python in the Python 3.12 smoke test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The nightly `(H200 MIG 18GB) [Nightly] Python 3.12 Smoke` job has failed in every build since #68457 switched it from Python 3.14 to 3.12. Triton can't build its driver stub: `fatal error: Python.h: No such file or directory`. This makes `python_only_compile.sh` ask uv for a managed interpreter, which ships the headers. Test-only change.

## Claims

- Fixes `Python 3.12 Smoke`: the CI script passes on the same image where it fails today.
- No change for the ROCm path or the non-smoke `python_only_compile.sh` runs.

## Validation

- CI failures on main:
  - [104240](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104240#01a1f29e-c265-438c-9445-6a35b88e8829)
  - [104395](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104395#01a1f532-cc57-4166-8ae7-8df55da2cc76)

  Both have `Using CPython 3.12.3 interpreter at: /usr/bin/python3.12`, then `Python.h: No such file or directory`, then `InductorError`, then `Engine core initialization failed`.
- **Setup:** ran the step's exact command in the CI image for main `d1ad1088bc` (`public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:d1ad1088bc63d5320689b06ba36fc5ae0564361f`, uv 0.13.9) on one B200 each, in two fresh containers.
  - `CI_STANDALONE_MERGE_BASE=898a7c68c2`, the newest main wheel published at the time. There are no `csrc/` changes between it and `d1ad1088bc`.

  ```bash
  cd /vllm-workspace/tests
  PYTHON_ONLY_COMPILE_PYTHON=3.12 bash standalone_tests/python_only_compile.sh
  ```

  main (exit 1):
  ```text
  + uv venv --python 3.12 /tmp/python-only-venv
  Using CPython 3.12.3 interpreter at: /usr/bin/python3.12
  .../triton/backends/nvidia/driver.c:9:10: fatal error: Python.h: No such file or directory
  torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: CalledProcessError: Command '['/usr/bin/gcc', '.../triton/backends/nvidia/driver.c', ... '-I/usr/include/python3.12']' returned non-zero exit status 1.
  RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
  ```

  this PR (exit 0):
  ```text
  + uv venv --python 3.12 --managed-python /tmp/python-only-venv
  Using CPython 3.12.16
  [shutdown] MPClient: complete
  + '[' '!' -f /tmp/changed.file ']'
  ```
- `shellcheck` with the repo's pre-commit arguments passes on the changed script.

## Details

- **Root cause:** #68457 made Python 3.14 the image default and moved this smoke step from 3.14 to 3.12. The image's Ubuntu 24.04 base ships `/usr/bin/python3.12` without development headers; the Dockerfile installs `python${PYTHON_VERSION}-dev`, which is now 3.14. By default uv prefers an already-installed interpreter that satisfies the request, so `uv venv --python 3.12` picks the system one. Under 3.14 there was no system 3.14, so uv downloaded its own build, which includes the headers. That's why the old smoke test passed.
- **Why not install `python3.12-dev`:** the smoke test is meant to check a Python version the image wasn't built for. A uv-managed interpreter keeps it independent of the image's apt packages.
- **ROCm:** the AMD mirror passes and uses its own branch of the script, so it's unchanged.
- **Not a duplicate:** GitHub search for `python_only_compile`, `Python.h` and "Python 3.12 Smoke" found no open PR (Nov 20).

AI assistance was used for this PR.
