commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Don't run chunked post-processing for /pooling
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `enable_chunked_processing`, every `/pooling` request to an embedding server fails with "Chunked embedding metadata not available". `/pooling` shares `EmbedIOProcessor` with `/v1/embeddings` but never chunks its inputs, while `post_process_online` picks the chunked aggregation from the server setting. This PR branches on whether the request was actually chunked instead. Fixes #67790.

Narrowed per review: `/pooling` does not run chunked processing; it behaves as on a non-chunked server.

## Claims

- `/pooling` works on embedding servers with `enable_chunked_processing`, with its usual `max_model_len` limit, and returns the same vector as `/v1/embeddings`.
- `/v1/embeddings` is unchanged: its preprocessing always sets the chunk metadata when chunked processing is enabled.

## Validation

RTX 4070 Laptop, main = `82c6b325b4`. New test in `tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online_long_text.py`, using the existing chunked-processing server (`intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`, `max_model_len` 512):

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online_long_text.py -k pooling_endpoint
```

```text
main:
E   requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 400 Client Error: Bad Request for url: http://127.0.0.1:45615/pooling
1 failed, 5 deselected in 31.04s

this PR:
1 passed, 5 deselected
```

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online_long_text.py \
       tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py      # 70 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py            # 22 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/basic/test_truncation.py        # 3 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/classify/test_online.py         # 17 passed
```

`pre-commit` passes.

## Details

- Root cause: only `ServingEmbedding._preprocessing` calls `maybe_pre_process_chunked`, so `/pooling` reaches `_post_process_chunked` without metadata. This dates from #46782.
- Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR mentions the error or `/pooling` with chunked processing; recent chunked-embedding fixes (#62859, #47696, #57035) touch other paths.

commits.pr_title: [Security] Reject ICNS image inputs before decoding
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Remove ICNS from the shared Pillow image allowlist. Requests that supply an Apple Icon Image file receive the existing invalid-image error. The multimodal guide directs callers to convert these files to PNG or JPEG.

## Claims

- The shared opener rejects ICNS before raster decoding.
- The regression tests cover bytes, local files, base64, and chat requests using valid icons.
- Existing raster-format tests continue to pass.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -q -k rejects_icns` failed on the base commit because the loader accepted ICNS.
- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py -q -k 'not video or jpeg'` passed 28 tests.
- The local CPU render endpoint returned HTTP 400 for ICNS and HTTP 200 for PNG with Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct. The health endpoint returned HTTP 200.
- Pre-commit passed for all changed files. The full chat-completions regression is included for CI.

## Details

The Pillow ICNS reader does not expose reliable decoded dimensions before loading. Excluding the format at the shared opener keeps the admission check consistent across the standard Python multimodal loader and its other callers.

The duplicate-work check covered open and merged decoder, allowlist, and budget changes. #60022 introduced the allowlist, #61226 introduced request-wide accounting, and #63369 retains Pillow as the default decoder. Those changes leave ICNS in the allowlist.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] QSA: sm_100 split-K launch configs for small batches
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`_qsa_sparse_paged_gqa_splitk_kernel` is the Triton split-K kernel that runs QSA sparse attention over each query's 2048 selected tokens. Its launch config (BLOCK_N, target_splits, num_warps) comes from `_select_config()` in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa.py`, a table tuned on GB300 (sm_103). sm_90 and sm_120 already have their own tables (vllm-project/vllm#57273, #55557), but sm_100 (B200, GB200) still uses the GB300 entries.

This PR adds `_select_sm100_config()`, a full table built the same way as `_select_sm90_config()`. It changes only the small-batch regions where B200 measures faster; every other region keeps the GB300 table's current values, so sm_100 no longer follows future GB300 retunes. Nothing changes on any other GPU.

## Claims

On B200, as kernel time per call (split-K + merge + fused output gate, CUDA graph, L2 flushed before each call):

- **fp8 K/V cache** (the recipe default on Blackwell) at 5–64 programs:
  - Latency drops 11–41%.
  - With TP4/TP8 + MTP3 (4 rows per request, 1 KV head per rank), this covers concurrency 2–16.
  - Above 64 programs, fp8 keeps taking the `qsa_fp8` kernel (vllm-project/vllm#66512), unchanged.
- **bf16 K/V cache** at ≤ 24 programs:
  - Latency drops 7–30% from 4 programs up.
  - At 1–2 programs it is neutral: −10% to +1%.
- **All other regions and GPUs:** unchanged. sm_103 (B300/GB300) keeps the table it was tuned on.
- **End to end:** no measurable change, as expected for a kernel that takes 3.6% of step time (7.9 ms of a 219.5 ms window at TEP4 + MTP3, concurrency 16, torch profiler on B200). Over two server starts per arm, mean per-step decode time is 0.2–1.0% lower at concurrency 1–16, but it is 1.0% lower at concurrency 1 too, where the table does not change, so this is within run-to-run noise. GSM8K is 0.966–0.969 either way.

## Validation

**Correctness:**

```
# one B200; qsa.py from main @ 5e921de215, rest of vLLM 0.34.0rc1.dev849+gb24eda712;
# the test file plus three local fp8 cases (see below)
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py \
  -k "test_qsa_sparse_paged_attention_correctness or test_qsa_fp8_kernel_correctness"
current qsa.py:  25 passed, 82 deselected in 34.96s
this PR:         25 passed, 82 deselected in 30.15s
```

- **What was run:**
  - `test_qsa_sparse_paged_attention_correctness` and `test_qsa_fp8_kernel_correctness` from `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`, on one B200.
  - Both the current `qsa.py` and this PR's version were tested.
  - The runs used only this test module plus a stub `tests/utils.py`, because vLLM's full test requirements were not installed on the test host. These two tests use no fixtures.
- **Local test cases:** no existing case reaches the fp8 regions this table changes. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix Qwen3-VL M-RoPE input positions after a pruned video
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--video-pruning-rate`, the Qwen3-VL processor puts the retained tokens of every frame of a video into the first frame's slot. `_get_mrope_input_positions` advanced the position counter only by the frame grids those tokens fill. Everything after the video got positions that are too early, and a video that keeps fewer tokens than one frame got a whole frame grid, so the result had more columns than the prompt has tokens. `MultiModalPruner.recompute` overwrites these positions when the video is encoded. It does not run when the video is a prefix cache hit, so on those requests the model reads the text after the video at the wrong positions. With this PR every frame advances the counter by one grid, as it does without pruning.

Fixes #68269. #67190 makes the same kind of fix for Qwen2.5-VL and leaves Qwen3-VL out of scope.

## Claims

For Qwen3-VL with `--video-pruning-rate` (EVS or VidCom2):

- The text and media after a pruned video, and the first generated token, get the positions they have without pruning. These are also the positions `_recompute_mrope_positions` gives them, so a request whose video is a prefix cache hit now uses the same positions as one where the video is encoded. Before, they were early by (T − ⌊n/P⌋)·max(h, w) − part(n mod P) positions (defined under Details). That is 120 positions for a 16-frame 960x544 video at rate 0.5 with the `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` processor.
- A video that keeps fewer tokens than one frame (VidCom2 at high rates or on short videos) gets one position per prompt token. Before, it got a whole frame grid.
- Nothing changes without pruning. The positions and the delta are identical for 1502 of 1502 random unpruned prompts, and the existing test in `test_qwen3_vl_mrope.py` still passes.

## Validation

This PR is based on main `f55dbdfb9d`; the diff was written against `5d83998e` and applies unchanged. Everything below ran on the nightly wheel of the base, `vllm-0.34.0rc1.dev751+gf55dbdfb9` (torch 2.14.0+cu130), once as installed and once with this PR's `qwen3_vl.py` swapped in; nothing else differs between the two. The unit tests need no GPU. The end-to-end test ran on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB). The unit tests also ran first on a v0.32.0 install, where the functions this PR touches and the code they call are byte-identical to `5d83998e` (`_get_mrope_input_positions`, `_iter_mm_grid_hw`, `_recompute_mrope_positions`, `get_video_replacement_qwen3vl`, `get_video_repl`, `evs.py`, `vidcom2.py`), with the same results.

### New tests

```bash
pytest -v tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_vl_mrope.py
```

| | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_vl_mrope.py`, base's nightly wheel | `46 failed, 114 passed in 34.37s` | `160 passed in 35.47s` |
| the same, v0.32.0 install | `46 failed, 114 passed in 5.29s` | `160 passed in 5.16s` |

The new tests are `test_get_mrope_input_positions_pruned_video` (60 cases) and `test_pruned_video_prefix_cache_hit_matches_recompute` (4 cases). The cases cover 4 grids × {unpruned, EVS 0.3, EVS 0.5, VidCom2 0.75, VidCom2 0.95} × {one video, two videos, image + video + image}. These include a lump with a partial frame, a lump of exactly one frame, a lump smaller than one frame, and a single-frame video. The 96 existing cases pass on both. The new tests need no GPU: with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""` they give `64 passed, 96 deselected`.

On the base, 42 + 4 of the new cases fail. All of them are pruned. The ones that pass on the base are the 12 unpruned cases and the 6 single-frame EVS cases, where EVS keeps the whole frame. 31 cases fail on positions and 15 on the column count. The 15 are the cases that keep fewer tokens than one frame.

<details>
<summary>Representative failures on the base</summary>

```
test_get_mrope_input_positions_pruned_video[video-evs0.5-12x34x60]
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
    Mismatched elements: 18 / 27 (66.7%)
    Greatest absolute difference: 180 at index (0, 3)
test_get_mrope_input_positions_pruned_video[video-evs0.3-12x34x60]
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
    Mismatched elements: 18 / 27 (66.7%)
    Greatest absolute difference: 90 at index (0, 3)
test_get_mrope_input_positions_pruned_video[video-vidcom2-0.95-12x34x60]
E   assert torch.Size([3, 579]) == (3, 375)
test_pruned_video_prefix_cache_hit_matches_recompute[0-12x34x60-evs0.3]
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
    Mismatched elements: 18 / 18 (100.0%)
    Greatest absolute difference: 90 at index (0, 0)
```

180 and 90 are the formula's values for 12 grids of 17x30 at EVS 0.5 (n = 3060 = 6·510) and at EVS 0.3 (n = 4284 = 8·510 + 204).

</details>

### Prompts from the real processor

These prompts were built with vLLM's processor for `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, using a 16-frame synthetic video (8 temporal grids). The table compares the positions of the text after the video, and of the first generated token, with the same prompt unpruned.

| Video | Pruning | Kept tokens | Base: text after the video is early by | Base: columns / tokens | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 960x544 (17x30 grid) | EVS 0.5 | 2040 | 120 | 2129 / 2129 | 0, first generated token at 329 as unpruned |
| 960x544 | EVS 0.3 | 2856 | 60 | 2945 / 2945 | 0 |
| 960x544 | VidCom2 0.5 | 2040 | 120 | 2129 / 2129 | 0 |
| 960x544 | VidCom2 0.95 | 204 | 297 to 317 | 599 / 293 | 0, 293 / 293 |
| 1280x720 (22x40 grid) | EVS 0.5 | 3520 | 160 | 3609 / 3609 | 0, first generated token at 409 as unpruned |
| 1280x720 | EVS 0.3 | 4928 | 80 | 5017 / 5017 | 0 |
| 1280x720 | VidCom2 0.5 | 3520 | 160 | 3609 / 3609 | 0 |
| 1280x720 | VidCom2 0.95 | 352 | 377 to 397 | 969 / 441 | 0, 441 / 441 |

On the base, the first generated token is at 209 instead of 329 for 960x544 at EVS 0.5, and at 249 instead of 409 for 1280x720 at EVS 0.5.

The next comparison uses the same processor, with a system prompt and the video placeholder written as in the chat template (inside `<|vision_start|> … <|vision_end|>`) and as a bare `<|video_pad|>`. It sets the cache-hit positions against the positions that `_recompute_mrope_positions` gives when the video is encoded, using two random sets of kept tokens. The table shows how many positions early the text after the video is:

| Placeholder | Pruning | Cache hit, base | Encoded, base and PR | Cache hit, PR | First generated position: unpruned / cache hit (base → PR) / encoded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chat template | EVS 0.5 | 120 | 0, 0 | 0 | 340 / 220 → 340 / 340 |
| chat template | VidCom2 0.95 | 297 | 0, 0 | 0 | 340 / 130 → 340 / 340 |
| bare | EVS 0.5 | 120 | 0, 0 | 0 | 338 / 218 → 338 / 338 |
| bare | VidCom2 0.95 | 297 | 0, 0 | 0 | 338 / 128 → 338 / 338 |

### 5000 random prompts

The prompts are seeded and random: 1 to 3 media items (videos and images), grids up to 24x24, spatial merge 1 or 2, random text and timestamp lengths, an optional chat-template wrapper, and either no pruning or a random method and rate. Retained counts come from `compute_retained_tokens_count`. Base against this PR:

- Unpruned (1502 prompts): positions and delta are identical for 1502 of 1502.
- Pruned (3498 prompts): this PR gives one column per token, the unpruned position for every token outside a pruned video, and the unpruned first generated position, for 3498 of 3498. The base does the same for 536 of them. For 372 it returns more columns than tokens.
- In the 727 pruned single-video prompts that keep at least one frame and have text after the video, the base is early by exactly (T − ⌊n/P⌋)·m − part(n mod P) in 727 of 727 (by up to 312 positions).

### Cost

`_get_mrope_input_positions` on one 64-frame 17x30 video prompt, best of 5×20 calls on CPU:

| | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unpruned (33138 tokens) | 0.804 ms | 0.722 ms |
| EVS 0.5 (16818 tokens) | 0.310 ms | 0.372 ms |

### End-to-end

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen3_vl.py -m core_model
```

`test_qwen3_vl_pruned_video_prefix_cache_hit` (new): `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, the `baby_reading` asset at 16 frames, prefix caching on. The same prompt runs twice. It has enough text after the video that the second request's cache hit covers the whole video, which the test asserts with `num_cached_tokens`. The greedy outputs of the two requests must match (`check_outputs_equal`).

| | unpruned (control) | EVS 0.5 | VidCom2 0.5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base | passed | failed | failed |
| This PR | passed | passed | passed |

Three runs of each arm gave the same result.

<details>
<summary>The base failures (cache miss / cache hit)</summary>

```
[evs-0.5]      'A baby wearing glasses sits on a bed, holding and turning a book, and then looks up and smiles.'
               'A baby wearing glasses sits on a bed, holding a book, and turns it over.'
[vidcom2-0.5]  'A baby wearing glasses sits on a bed, reading a book and turning the pages.'
               'A baby wearing glasses sits on a bed, opens a book, and reads it.'
```

</details>

The test compares tokens, not `check_logprobs_close`. On the base the cache hit diverges after 9 to 12 tokens, but each diverging token is in the other request's top 5, so `check_logprobs_close` passes on the base. Measured outside the test with 128 max tokens, both methods, 16 and 32 frames:

- base: diverges at token 9 to 12, with a largest \|Δlogprob\| of 0.55 to 0.88 on the common prefix;
- this PR: identical tokens, with a largest \|Δlogprob\| of 0.03 to 0.08;
- unpruned: identical tokens on both, 0.049 (the cache-hit noise floor).

The prompt leaves out the chat template's outer `<|vision_start|>`/`<|vision_end|>` pair; the processor wraps every frame itself. With the outer pair, the cache-miss path is itself wrong on main (#62937, fixed by #62959). After a short prefix, as here, the first request raises `RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (0) must match the existing size (949)`, on the base and with this PR alike.

Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 MoE checkpoints (`Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`) could not be checked on main: any pruned request raises `AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'video_pruning_method'` (#54208, open).

<details>
<summary>Where this was found (out-of-tree, not this PR's code)</summary>

The setup was a video QA workload on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, with `video_pruning_rate` 0.5 (VidCom2), prefix caching, and a local equivalent of #54208's `video_pruning_method` fix. Because the shared prefix is block-aligned, most follow-up questions about the same clip are whole-video prefix cache hits. A local prompt-time correction shifted the positions after the lumped video by the formula under Details. With it, a GPU read-back of the consumed positions matched the unpruned layout for 655 of 655 whole-video prefix hits. Before the correction, the mean |ΔP(yes)| between cold and warm calls of the same question was 0.030, against a warm-warm floor of 0.019. After it, the mean was 0.020, against a floor of 0.021 (64 clip/question pairs). This PR's code was not run there.

</details>

### Lint

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.17.2, as pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) and `typos` (v1.51.1) pass on both files, as do the repository's Python hooks that apply to them (SPDX header, docstring style, forbidden strings, `torch.cuda` calls, boolean context managers, test tethering, trust-remote-code). `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` (mypy 1.20.2) reports no new errors in the two files. The full `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` (as in the pre-commit workflow, with `SKIP=pip-compile`) passes: 31 hooks passed, the 8 pip-compile hooks skipped, and no file changed. On the new e2e test file, 16 hooks pass, including `check-test-tethering`.

## Details

**Root cause.** With pruning, `get_video_replacement_qwen3vl` writes `tokens_per_frame = [num_tokens] + [0] * (num_frames - 1)` ([qwen3_vl.py L1608](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5d83998e927f3081c804932e6586bd7312a424e8/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1608)). Which tokens are kept is known only after encoding. `_get_mrope_input_positions` ([L2791-L2864](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5d83998e927f3081c804932e6586bd7312a424e8/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py#L2791-L2864)) handled this layout in three ways:

- frames with no tokens were skipped, so they advanced the counter by nothing;
- a lump of n tokens was laid out on ⌊n/P⌋ full grids plus a partial grid;
- a lump of at most one frame took the `else` branch, which emits a whole grid whatever the token count.

The text tokens (timestamps, `<|vision_start|>`, `<|vision_end|>`) are the same in both layouts. So the only difference is the grid advance: T·m without pruning, ⌊n/P⌋·m + part(r) with it. Here P = h·w tokens per frame on the merged grid, m = max(h, w), r = n mod P, and part(r) is the largest offset in a partial grid of r cells plus one: max(⌊(r−1)/w⌋, min(r, w) − 1) + 1, or 0 when r = 0. For n ≥ P, everything after the video was therefore early by (T − ⌊n/P⌋)·m − part(r). For n < P, the `else` branch emitted P columns for n tokens. The formula depends only on n, T, h and w. n in turn depends only on the method, the rate and the grid (`compute_retained_tokens_count`), not on the content.

When the video is encoded, `MultiModalPruner.recompute` rewrites the positions from the video on. Text after the video continues after the largest position of the video's tokens, which is the last `<|vision_end|>` at its unpruned position. The recompute is skipped for a request whose scheduled window has no media embeddings (`if num_req_embeds == 0: continue`, [GPU runner L74](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5d83998e927f3081c804932e6586bd7312a424e8/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mm_pruning.py#L74), [CPU runner L61](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5d83998e927f3081c804932e6586bd7312a424e8/vllm/v1/worker/cpu/mm_pruning.py#L61)). A whole-video prefix cache hit is such a request, and so is a hit that ends inside the video item after the last retained token (all retained tokens sit in the first frame's slot, and `_num_window_embeds` counts only embedding rows). It then uses the positions and the delta as `_get_mrope_input_positions` returned them.

**Fix.** Each frame advances the counter by one grid (m), whatever its token count. The lumped tokens keep their layout on consecutive grids, starting where they started before. A lump smaller than one frame now gets one position per token. As a result, every token except the retained tokens of a pruned video gets its unpruned position, and so does the first generated token. That includes the later frames' timestamp and vision-marker tokens, which a hit ending inside the video item uses as computed here: in a CPU check of 96 such hits (hit 1 to 15 tokens before the end of the video item), all match the unpruned layout with this PR and none on the base. The tests check the tokens outside the video and the first generated position, and do not pin positions inside the video. The fix also drops the `NOTE: this should never be the case` remainder comment: a partial last grid is the common case (EVS 0.3 on 8 grids of 17x30 keeps 2856 = 5·510 + 306 tokens).

**Scope.**

- Only Qwen3-VL's `_get_mrope_input_positions` changes. Subclasses that inherit it get the change too (Qwen3-VL-MoE, InternS1-Pro, Cosmos3, ColQwen3, Alpamayo2Super, and the Qwen3.5 ConditionalGeneration classes, where pruning also needs #54208). So does Cosmos3-Edge, which calls it directly. None of them changes without pruning.
- `recompute_mrope_positions` is untouched. When a prefix cache hit ends before the last retained video token, the recompute runs from there and is wrong for its own reasons (#62969). #62959 takes the base from the position of the token before the placeholder. For the first media item that position is unchanged here. For an item after a pruned video, it is one of the positions this PR corrects. The combination was not run.
- Not addressed: the integer positions travel in the bfloat16 embedding tensor and are rounded above 256 (#68268), and the outer-marker anchoring is #62937.

- PR and main builds no longer schedule this step by default.

## Overview

Add online re-quantization of ModelOpt NVFP4 linear weights while retaining the ModelOpt checkpoint loader. Support MXFP4 shorthand and target-based conversion.

## Claims

- Dequantize serialized ModelOpt NVFP4 linear weights, including partition-specific global scales, before applying the selected online quantization method.
- Resolve `--quantization mxfp4` after detecting a ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint. Explicit quantization settings override shorthand defaults; `targets` applies only to matching layers.
- Allow supported weight-conversion targets on platforms while leaving untargeted checkpoint layers on their existing quantization path.
- Document target selection, configuration behavior, and model-specific accuracy considerations.

## Validation

- **Targeted tests:** 67 passed, covering weight loading, TP partitioning, shorthand resolution, targets, ignore behavior, LM-head selection, and platform validation.
- **XPU smoke:** Ripple-65B-Preview-NVFP4, revision `2789217ba87d93e8d032fad25217c4c63a0e1d5b`, TP=4, `quantization="mxfp4"` and `targets={"*mlp*":"mxfp4"}`. Selected `XPUMxFp4LinearKernel` and generated `4.` for “What is 2 + 2? Answer briefly.”

commits.pr_title: [RL][Model Loader] Reload directly by default with weight updates (VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=auto)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Makes direct weight reload (#64336) the default for engines with runtime weight updates (`weight_transfer_config`), part of #54477. Plain serving is identical to main. The design is aoshen02's (aoshen02/vllm#336).

`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE` gets a third value, `auto`, which becomes the default:

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | Direct reload where it applies (rule below), else layerwise. Fallbacks never raise; each one is logged. |
| `direct` | Main's meaning: direct reload always, and unsupported configs and models raise. One exception: a model loaded from pre-processed weights (and its draft) falls back to layerwise with a log instead of raising. |
| `layerwise` | Main's meaning: always layerwise. |

The `auto` rule:
- The engine reloads directly only if it has a `weight_transfer_config`, its backend is not `sharded_rdt` or `sparse_nccl`, the config isn't one direct reload refuses (weight offloading, torchao, `draft_lm_head_quantization`), and LoRA is off. Otherwise every model reloads layerwise.
- At cold start a model still reloads layerwise if it has online-quantized or Humming modules or was loaded from pre-processed weights.
- A draft reloads layerwise whenever its target does (they may share tensors): the model runner decides this before the draft loads and logs it. Otherwise the draft decides like any model.
- Each fallback is logged once per rank with its reason.
- Under `auto` online quantization keeps its online methods (quantize-on-load stays a `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` feature), so online-quantized engines reload layerwise as on main.
- With a transfer config, disk `reload_weights` is also direct under `auto`, and like every direct update it must load every weight.

## Changes

- `vllm/envs.py`: `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE` accepts `auto`, `layerwise`, `direct`; default `auto`.
- `vllm/config/vllm.py`: the config checks move into a `VllmConfig.direct_reload_refusal()` method next to `_verify_direct_reload_compat`, which returns the reason. `_verify_direct_reload_compat` still raises at startup with that reason under `direct`; `auto` uses the reason to fall back.
- `reload/direct.py`:
  - `direct_reload_enabled()` now means "a model loaded now records its checkpoint layout": `direct`, or `auto` with no config refusal (`config.direct_reload_refusal()`, plus `sparse_nccl` and LoRA under `auto`), and not inside `layerwise_draft()`.
  - `record_checkpoint_layout` decides the model's mode once at cold start: pre-processed weights or a module refusal (`_module_refusal`: online quantization, including methods behind wrappers such as input Hadamard, and Humming) leave it layerwise. Under `direct` a module refusal still raises at load.
  - `reloads_directly(model)` is the per-model mode: the model has a recorded checkpoint layout.
  - `layerwise_draft()` is a context the model runner (`v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) enters to load the draft when the target has no recorded layout, so the draft reloads layerwise too.
  - Every fallback logs through one helper, once per rank.
- Callers use the per-model mode instead of the env var: `start_reload`/`finish_reload` (`lifecycle.py`), the load plan's `check_plannable` (its error is now `load plan: requires direct reload; this rank reloads layerwise (see its startup log)`), the worker's failed-finish handling (`gpu_worker.py`; a failed finish now always ends the session, since neither mode can retry it), and `replace_parameter`'s `whole_storage`, now set only for tensors with a recorded checkpoint layout.
- Docs (`direct_reload.md`, `layerwise.md`, `weight_transfer/README.md`) and the NCCL `use_load_plan` docstrings describe the new default.
- Tests: `test_direct_reload_enabled` covers the `auto` rule (updates, no updates, LoRA, `sparse_nccl`); `test_auto_refused_model_and_its_draft_reload_layerwise` covers a refused model reloading layerwise and a draft loaded under `layerwise_draft()` reloading layerwise without its own checks (also under `direct`); the online-quantization refusal test also covers a wrapped method; the worker's failed-finish test now expects the session to end. `test_reload_refit.py` now runs in the default mode, and existing tests are adjusted to the per-model mode.

## Test Plan

GB200, nightly wheel with each arm's Python files overlaid, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE` unset (so `auto` on the PR, `layerwise` on main).
- Gate (job 52561, PR db755ff835 vs main b582592d5a, same base), Qwen3-0.6B, greedy: plain BF16 and online fp8 without updates (quant methods, KV blocks, outputs vs main); with `weight_transfer_config`: BF16, LoRA, online fp8, each with a reload. Test suites on both arms.
- Perf (job 52533, at cd1721f3cb; the PR's commits since only change how the mode is decided, not the reload path it measures): Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 BF16, TP2, `{"backend":"nccl"}`, 1 warm-up + 3 timed full updates (56.9 GiB), default vs `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise`.

## Test Result

**End to end (job 52561)**

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| BF16, no updates | identical to main: same methods, 7264 KV blocks, same outputs |
| online fp8, no updates | identical to main: same methods, 7336 KV blocks, same outputs |
| BF16, updates | direct reload ok |
| LoRA, updates | layerwise reload ok, fallback logged |
| online fp8, updates | layerwise reload ok, fallback logged |

**Suites (job 52561).** Every failure also fails on main, with exactly the same set (environment: HF snapshots not cached on this cluster, DeepGEMM unavailable, a PTX toolchain mismatch).

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py` | 19 passed |
| `test_weight_transfer.py` | 141 passed, 23 skipped |
| direct reload suites | the same 2 failures as main |
| `test_keep_param_objects.py` | the same 8 failures as main |
| `test_online.py`, `test_online_loading.py` | the same 20 failures as main |
| `test_reload.py`, `test_reload_moe_kernels.py` | the same 21 failures as main |
| `test_reload_refit.py` | the same 12 failures as main |
| draft weight reload | the same 2 failures as main |

**Full weight update (job 52533).** Time on the slower rank; peak is allocated GPU memory above the pre-update baseline. Outputs equal across modes; 41,600 KV blocks in both.

| Mode | Update times (s) | Median (s) | Peak extra GPU mem (GiB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (`auto` → direct) | 2.40 / 2.48 / 2.51 | 2.48 | 1.30 |
| `layerwise` | 4.41 / 4.45 / 4.47 | 4.45 | 2.69 |

Online-quantized engines stay layerwise under `auto`, so no fp8 numbers apply.

## Limitations

- **Pipeline parallel:** stages decide per model, so when refused modules sit on some stages only, the stages can pick different modes. The load plan then refuses on the layerwise ranks, pointing to their startup log.
- **Components silently wrong under direct reload aren't refused here.** #66002 lists DSV4 AITER MegaMoE, Step-5 MegaMoE, DSV4 AMD monokernel decode, MiniMax-M3 AMD mono decode and Qwen3.8 PLE disk offload. With weight updates they now get direct reload by default; use `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise` for them until #66002 lands.
- **Loader-bypass audit not done.** A full audit of `vllm/models/**` for writes that bypass weight loaders is tracked as F12 on the #54477 tracker. It applies to explicit `direct` with online quantization; `auto` keeps online quantization layerwise.
- **LoRA** reloads layerwise under `auto` (a LoRA model's `lm_head` is not loaded again by every update).
- **Draft edge cases.** Both fail loudly at the draft's first update; use `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise` for them:
  - a direct target whose checkpoint-quantized lm_head is re-laid out by post-load processing and shared by an EAGLE/MTP draft;
  - a draft with its own config-level quantization such as torchao (config refusals are checked against the target's config).
- **At TP > 1 a refused update RPC can take the engine down** (other ranks' replies stay queued and the next RPC reads them; #60401, still open). Under `auto` refusals become layerwise fallbacks, so this only applies to explicit `direct` and the load-plan refusal above.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Engram pool: split Engram tables across engines over NVLink or RDMA
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `vllm/distributed/engram_pool/`, a pool of read-only tables split by rows over every GPU of a group of engines. Rows move over NVLink, or over RDMA from HBM or host memory. DeepSeek V4.1's cross-engine peer group (#66552) now runs on it and gains `peer_group_transport: nvlink | rdma`.

Same goal as RFC #64002, #64395, #57023 and #64082 (one copy of the Engram tables shared across engines), different approach: no owner host or process, no native dependency (verbs through ctypes), NVLink and RDMA from HBM or host memory, and fetches fully capturable in CUDA graphs. Tracking issue: #57448.

## Design

- **NVLink:** every GPU maps every shard (cuMem FABRIC); a fetch is one gather kernel.
- **RDMA:** the owner's NIC gathers rows, ~15 rows (one packet) per RDMA WRITE, so fetches are not bound by the NIC's READ message rate. The requester's GPU writes the WRs and posts the request itself (mlx5 WQE + doorbell); a per-GPU owner proxy process posts them on its NIC. Each QP's last chain ends with a READ and a fenced flag WRITE, and the consumer kernel waits on the flags. A fetch is 2 kernels, with no host sync.
- **Engines sharing NICs:** another engine's prefill could fill every owner QP and delay decode fetches (P/D in one group). `peer_group_rdma_inflight` (default 8) bounds prefill-sized gathers in flight per NIC.

- **Host shards:** placed on the GPU's NUMA node. Same-node peers map them and gather with their own NIC, so no same-node QPs are needed (rail-optimized fabrics work). `peer_group_thp_dir` (a `huge=always` tmpfs) puts them on transparent huge pages, which the NIC translates far less often.

Prefill and decode engines can share one group (each GPU holds less) or use one group each (no interference, a full copy per group). The DP ranks of one engine step together, so the bound does not matter within one engine.

## Validation

GB200 NVL72, 2 nodes x 4 GPUs (4x 400G RoCE per node), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, two DEP4 engines in one 8-GPU group.

**Tests.** `pytest -q tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/test_config.py -k 'engram or pool'`: 134 passed. Pool lookups are checked exactly against a full-table reference over NVLink, RDMA from HBM, and RDMA from host memory, including CUDA graph replays. pre-commit passes.

**Fetch latency** (both layers, 24 rows/token/layer, 264 B rows, real tables (2 x 384M rows), 8 GPUs fetching at once, CUDA graph, every fetch checked byte for byte):

| Tokens per GPU | NVLink | RDMA, host shards | RDMA, HBM shards |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.017 ms | 0.184 ms | 0.190 ms |
| 64 | 0.019 ms | 0.193 ms | 0.202 ms |
| 512 | 0.029 ms | 0.412 ms | 0.276 ms |
| 2K | 0.077 ms | 1.29-1.40 ms | 0.857 ms |
| 8K | 0.257 ms | 5.3-6.9 ms | 3.58 ms |
| 32K | 0.970 ms | 25.9 ms | 18.9 ms |

The previous commit (7532a201) measured the same in the same allocation (host shards, 8K: 6.9 ms). Tables of 32M rows fetch faster from host shards (8K: 3.4 ms in the same allocation), likely from NIC address translation misses over the larger shards, even on GB200's 64 KB pages. On B300 (4 KB pages, one 400G NIC per GPU), host shards fetch 8K tokens in 9.6 ms on base pages and 3.1 ms with `peer_group_thp_dir`.

The fetch starts before layer 0, so it overlaps compute: decode on-stream GPU cost is ~32 us per step.

**Model step overhead** (`vllm bench forward`, real tables (2 x 384M rows), RDMA host shards, two DEP4 engines in one 8-GPU group; the same steps with the fetch skipped as control, one value per node):

| Step | Step time | Fetch vs skipped |
|---|---|---|
| decode, 16 requests | 10.8 ms | +14 us (+0.1%, one node) |
| mixed, 16 requests, 2063 tokens | 49 ms | +66 / +307 us (+0.1-0.6%) |
| prefill, 2K tokens | 45 ms | +92 / +374 us (+0.2-0.8%) |
| prefill, 8K tokens | 117 ms | +240 / -869 us (noise) |

Sample spread is 0.3-1.3% per case, so every difference is within noise.

**Prefill and decode engines sharing owners** (`vllm bench forward`: one node runs 8K prefill steps back to back, the other times decode steps of 16 requests per rank):

| | Decode step |
|---|---|
| no Engram fetch | 10846 us |
| fetch, `peer_group_rdma_inflight=0` (no bound) | 11914 us (+9.9%) |
| fetch, bound 4 | 10870 us (+0.2%) |

At the default bound of 8, decode steps drop the same way against no bound (11809 -> 10873 us, a separate run), decode fetches drop from 0.41 to 0.22 ms p50, and the 8K prefill fetch keeps its rate (2.56 vs 2.5-2.6 ms p50).

**Serving** (both engines at once, c64, 2048 in / 256 out): NVLink 8730 output tok/s; RDMA host shards 8497-8703 over 5 runs, within run-to-run noise (+-1.5%).

**GSM8K** (lm_eval, 5-shot, greedy, strict-match), RDMA host shards: 0.928 / 0.927.

## Limitations

- RDMA needs mlx5 NICs (the GPU writes mlx5 WQEs). Peers exchange memory keys at startup, so the network must be trusted.
- With host shards, the engines of one node must run as one user in one PID namespace (peers open each other's shards through `/proc/<pid>/fd`).
- Requires CUDA SM89+ (FP8 dequant in the lookup kernel).
- TP=1 and PP=1, as in #66552. Weights cannot be reloaded; restarting one engine means restarting the group.
- Only DeepSeek V4.1 uses the pool so far.
- CI runners have neither IMEX nor RDMA, so the pool tests skip there; they ran on GB200 as above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Tile QSA indexer scoring and skip invisible columns
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The AMD QSA indexer scoring kernel now skips page-table columns past each request's visible range and scores 16 rows x 64 keys per program with `tl.dot`. It runs on every arch and cuts TTFT by 40–50% on MI355X and MI325X. Only gfx942 decode batches of ≤ 32 single-row requests keep the one-row kernel, which gets the same column skip.

## Claims

- On MI355X (TP2, MXFP4, no MTP), the PR raises output throughput by **1.62x** geometric mean across 12 cells. The range is +12% to +110%, with the largest gains at long context and high concurrency. Mean TTFT drops by about 50% in every cell.
- On MI325X (TP2, FP8, no MTP), the same sweep shows **1.43x** geometric mean output throughput. The range is +11% to +72%, and mean TTFT drops by 41–46% in every cell.
- On MI325X, the full selection (scoring, top-k and expand) at 32K and 98K context is 1.6x to 9.8x faster for batches of 64 (1.6x is 98K with one row per request).
- Accuracy is unchanged on both: GSM8K is within noise and NIAH-2 at 64K and 128K stays at 1.0.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** MI325X, head 8eb3fc0, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (0.34.0rc1.dev776+g7c3a9302f, triton 3.8.0) with `amd/ops/qsa.py`, `amd/qsa_indexer.py` and `tests/` mounted (file hash checked in the container):

    pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py   # 41 passed in 18-29 s (3 runs)
    pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare.py   # 32 passed, 16 skipped in 22.8 s

The new scoring test, `test_qsa_mqa_paged_matches_reference`, is one parametrized test with 12 cases: 4 cases × bf16/fp16/fp8.
- **Cases:** a mixed prefill/decode/empty 16-row block on the tiled kernel, and 1, 32 or 33 single-row decode requests. Up to 32 rows run on the gfx942 one-row kernel; 33 rows run on the tiled kernel.
- **Checks:** which kernel ran, `visible_blocks`, and the logits on visible columns against a torch reference.

Mutation checks on that test:
- one-row kernel visible bound −1: 6 of 12 cases fail (decode1, decode32);
- tiled kernel visible bound −1: 6 fail (mixed, decode33);
- tiled early exit −1 column: 3 fail (mixed, whose widest row sees 257 columns).

End-to-end numbers below were measured by @mjkvaak-amd ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62589#issuecomment-7002100225)) with `qsa.py` and `qsa_indexer.py` from 348ca71. Since then, the scoring kernel changed only in the fp8 indexer path (native fp8 dot, see Details). These runs use the default bf16 indexer KV cache, so they are unaffected; the bf16 scoring kernel times are unchanged at 8eb3fc0.

**End to end on MI355X (gfx950):**

- Baseline: stock `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-7c3a9302f5ac2441ad199134129e973d22a46797` .
- This PR: the same image with `amd/ops/qsa.py` and `amd/qsa_indexer.py` from 348ca71 patched in.
- Load comes from `sglang.bench_serve --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0.8`, with a fixed seed per cell.
- Each value is the median of 3 passes. The passes agree within 0.8%, and the PR was faster in 3 of 3 passes in every cell.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --revision b2091c3809eb51902f46a163973362d8176f9e58 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching \

```

**No accuracy regressions**.

## Details

- **Motivation:** `_qsa_mqa_paged_kernel` scored every row against the full page-table width (`max_model_len / 4` = 65,600 columns), however few were visible. In a 32K prefill on MI325X that was 43% of GPU time. Prefill chunks no longer pay for invisible columns, which is where the end-to-end gains come from. At 1-row decode, median ITL moves by less than 1%.
- **Dispatch:** `QSAIndexer._select` sets `single_row_decode = num_prefills == 0 and decode_query_len == 1`. Both are host values, so there is no device sync, and the choice is fixed at CUDA graph capture. The one-row kernel runs only on gfx942 (`get_cdna_version() == 3`) and only for at most 32 rows, the crossover on MI325X. Everything else uses the tiled kernel: prefill, mixed batches, MTP and gfx950. Either kernel is correct for any row-to-request mapping, so a wrong flag costs only speed.
- **Dot dtype:** `tl.dot` runs in the query dtype. q and the compressed-key cache always share the indexer dtype (bf16 by default, fp8 with `indexer_kv_dtype="fp8"` in the attention config).
  - bf16 and fp16 compile as before.
  - fp8 uses the fp8 MFMA instead of upcasting to bf16. Scoring kernel, MI325X, median of 5 × `do_bench`, old → new:
    - decode: 32K 64×4 126 → 99 µs, 98K 64×1 155 → 109 µs, 262K 64×4 386 → 283 µs;
    - prefill: 8K rows at 32K 2049 → 1941 µs.
  - bf16 is within 1%.
  - Not checked on gfx950.
- **No K ≥ 16 clamp:** the AMD backend in Triton 3.8 has no minimum `tl.dot` size (`get_min_dot_size` returns `(1, 1, 1)` and falls back to FMA). head_dim 4 and 8 match the reference on MI325X. Production head_dim is 128.
- **Logits past `visible_blocks[row]`** are undefined. The tiled kernel writes `-inf` there when another row in its block sees further. The only consumer, `top_k_per_row_decode`, reads `[0, visible_blocks[row])`.
- **Limitation:** single-row decode at 262K context with 64 requests goes from 353 to 368 µs (+4%) in the MI325X microbenchmark. This shape does not fit in TP2 KV, which holds about 9.35M tokens against the 16.8M needed.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Enable SM90 MXFP4 MegaMoE via FlashInfer MoE-EP
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` now runs MXFP4 MoE checkpoints, such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, on Hopper. It uses FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 x FP8 MegaMoE (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4843) through the existing FlashInfer MoE-EP adapter. The packed MXFP4 weights go to the kernel as loaded, without a bf16 round trip.

- Rebased onto main `2440ffc3870c`, which includes merged #62603, #64061 and the SM107 path from #65974. The incremental diff is six files, with +92/−48 production lines.
- Main pins FlashInfer 0.7.4. [#4843](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4843) shipped in 0.7.3, the minimum the adapter already requires.
- This answers the question in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62603#issuecomment-6460588074: it is an MXFP4-resident Hopper moe_ep entry, and it applies to an unmodified DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint.

Related:
- #64061 is merged and provides the native `deep_gemm_mega_moe` backend. The head-to-head results below use its earlier revision `335cff32bf`, measured on 2026-10-28. This PR provides the FlashInfer MoE-EP backend choice for the same weight format.
- #54032: FlashInfer's CUTLASS Humming grouped-GEMM MoE for the same quantization. It is not a megakernel.

## Claims

The following historical results were collected on 2026-10-28 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x H200. They compare main `77f58e5304`'s default MXFP4 backend (HUMMING with block-FP8 activations and `allgather_reducescatter`), the FlashInfer arm at `db751d56eb`, and #64061 at `335cff32bf`.

- **Decode** (DP8/EP8, 128K/512, DSpark3 with synthetic acceptance): +8% to +18% output throughput and -6% to -13% TPOT p50 at concurrency 32 to 192. No resolved change at concurrency 8.
- **Prefill** (DP4/EP4 at the full 1M context, 2048/1, natural DSpark3): +3.5% saturated throughput and lower TTFT p50 at every offered rate.
- **#64061 at `335cff32bf`**, on the same workload: +12% to +21% in decode, but -8.7% in prefill.
- **GSM8K** shows no resolved difference among the three backends.
- The backend is opt-in. Default backends do not change.

## Validation

### Rebase validation — 2026-11-18

Head `8eae63643d` on main `2440ffc3870c`, with FlashInfer 0.7.3, PyTorch 2.14.0 and Triton 3.8.0. The conflicts were with the SM107 NVFP4 path from #65974 in the adapter, the experts class and the kernel test, and both paths are kept. Pre-commit passes. The CPU/API command from the section below gives:

```text
======================= 48 passed, 36 skipped in 10.52s ========================
```

The additional cases come from tests added on main since the previous base. Native vLLM extensions were reused from the `329f93e190` build.

`50a1db871e` makes the SM90 MXFP4 config a required import: FlashInfer 0.7.3 always ships it, so the separate missing-kernel error and its two test skips are gone. The last commit adds a check to the SM90 GPU test: after weight processing, the layer's scale parameters are the kernel's per-block scales.

The Hopper GPU matrix (the `-k sm90_init_warmup` command below, four H200) passes at this head:

```text
================ 16 passed, 31 deselected in 832.78s (0:13:52) =================
```

### Review cleanup validation — 2026-11-13

CPU/API validation uses head `f9a2af3e3e` on main `5916cef98eed`, with FlashInfer 0.7.3, PyTorch 2.14.0 and Triton 3.8.0. All six changed files on the CPU validation tree hash-match this head. Pre-commit passes.

The format selector checks SM90 for both block-FP8 and MXFP4. Support checks query capability once and report the FlashInfer DeepGEMM kernel constraint separately. The shared API and MXFP4 feature errors name FlashInfer 0.7.3. Alias comments explain the storage invariant for supported EPLB paths.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' /opt/venv214/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py
```

```text
================== 35 passed, 32 skipped, 1 warning in 10.35s ==================
```

The 32 skipped cases require Hopper or Blackwell GPUs. The extended diagnostic test fails on `d3b4df7af7` with the new kernel-specific reason assertion and passes on this head. Reproducer is `pytest -v -s tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py -k mxfp4_weights_run_packed_on_hopper_without_eplb`.

The Hopper GPU matrix uniformly covers four expert geometries × two weight formats × EP2/EP4, for sixteen cases. The complete matrix passed on H200 on 2026-11-12 at `380a64b7b7`, as shown below. A subsequent ten-case check at `d3b4df7af7` also passed. These tests cover weight processing, the modular kernel, an idle rank and CUDA graph replay.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 /opt/venv214/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k sm90_init_warmup
```

```text
================ 16 passed, 25 deselected in 856.47s (0:14:16) =================
```

Native vLLM extensions were reused from the existing `eafe6af27610` build. The serving and GSM8K results below retain their original 2026-10-28 revisions and measurement date.

### Serving measurements — 2026-10-28

**Setup.**
- vLLM main 77f58e5304, on the native build of the 1cb31be702 nightly wheel. Between those two commits, csrc, cmake, setup and requirements are identical.
- All arms use FlashInfer nightly 0.7.2.dev20261027, torch 2.14.0+cu130, and DeepGEMM#44 at f4685f201e.
- Arms:
  - main: default backend.
  - main + #64061 (335cff32bf): `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`.
  - main + #62603 + this PR: `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`.
  - The trees differ only in each PR's files. The measured FlashInfer arm's 12 files hash-match the original `db751d56eb` branch.
- Order is serial on the same GPUs: main A1, #64061, this PR, main A2. "main" is the mean of the A1 and A2 medians.
- Client: `vllm-rs bench serve` with token-ID prompts.

**Prefill.**

|---:|---:|---:|---:|

One standard error is about 0.8 points, so no difference is resolved.

**Tests.** On H200 with FlashInfer 0.7.2.dev20261027:

```bash

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py   # CPU: 9 passed
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py -k sm90_init_warmup
# SM90 GPU: 16 passed (MXFP4 and block FP8, 4 expert shapes x EP2/EP4)
```

- The SM90 GPU test is exact on grid inputs. It covers the GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Kimi-K3 and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next expert shapes.
- For MXFP4 it runs with DeepSeek-V4 routing, which exercises the output view, the workspaces, an idle rank and a CUDA graph replay.
- The GPU cases require at least two Hopper GPUs, `nvshmem4py` and FlashInfer 0.7.3 or newer. The local GPU validation commands are listed above.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

Every server runs with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. The main arm omits `--moe-backend`; the #64061 arm passes `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`.

The loader is `safetensors` with prefetch for all arms. `fastsafetensors` OOMs here: it allocates a 94.6 GiB transient device buffer on top of 51.8 GiB of parameters.

```bash
# Decode
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}' \
  --load-format safetensors --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.8,0.6,0.5]}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl

vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 512 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((2 * C)) --seed 0

# Prefill
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0}' \
  --load-format safetensors --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl

# warm-up: --num-prompts 64 --seed 100; saturation: --seed 102, 104, 106
vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --num-prompts 1000 --seed 102
# Poisson: R in 20.2 28.3 32.4 36.4 40.5 44.5, N = round(60 * R), seeds 200 to 205
vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate $R --num-prompts $N --seed $SEED

# GSM8K, on each prefill server
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port $PORT
```
</details>

## Details

- **Weights.**
  - The MXFP4 oracle keeps the checkpoint's packed E2M1 bytes and E8M0 scales on Hopper. The adapter hands them to FlashInfer as `PrequantizedMoEWeights`.
  - FlashInfer interleaves gate/up rows and folds the scales into its kernel layout, an 11-exponent window per expert; it does not requantize.
  - On Blackwell nothing changes: the CuTeDSL kernel still gets bf16 and requantizes to NVFP4.
- **Activations.**
  - The kernel quantizes activations to E4M3 with one scale per token, and its fc2 input with one scale per 64 channels.
  - main's default uses block-FP8 (1x128) activations, so the arms are not bit-identical. GSM8K shows no resolved difference.
- **Adapter.**
  - `FlashInferMoeEp` takes the Hopper weight format (`"fp8_block"` or `"mxfp4"`) instead of a block-FP8 flag.
  - The MXFP4 path reuses #62603's 64/256/1024-token workspaces. With DeepSeek-V4 routing they now combine with FlashInfer's output view. FlashInfer selects workspace capacity and output ownership independently through `workspace` and `return_workspace_view`. [FlashInfer API](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.7.3/flashinfer/moe_ep/modes/mega_layer.py)
  - The kernel requires int64 expert ids, so the adapter converts top-k ids to the kernel's index dtype. This is one device-side cast per layer; nothing new reads back to the host.
- **Limitations.**
  - EPLB is rejected for MXFP4 on Hopper, because FlashInfer keeps a per-expert FP32 scale of these weights outside the layer's parameters.
  - Input-side router weights are rejected, as for block FP8: the kernel weights the activation before fc2.
  - `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` supports Blackwell. The native `deep_gemm_mega_moe` Hopper path is provided by merged #64061.
  - MXFP4 on Hopper requires FlashInfer 0.7.3 or newer, which ships the SM90 MXFP4 MegaMoE ([#4843](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4843)).
- **Versus #64061 at `335cff32bf`.** In the historical comparison, DeepGEMM's decode throughput leads by 2% to 10%, with the smallest gap at C=192. FlashInfer reaches 41.8 saturated prefill req/s versus 36.9. These measurements use the earlier revisions listed above. Both implementations are available as explicit backend choices.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Fast Start] Keep the source daemon up when the compiled cache cannot be published
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #63753 (compiled-cache seeding), part of #56049. If the compiled cache can't be bundled or published, for example because it exceeds the 8 GiB bundle limit, the `vllm preload` source daemon now keeps running. It serves weights and advertises no bundle, and targets compile locally.

## Claims

- **Oversized cache or failed publish.** The source daemon used to exit during warmup when its FlashInfer compiled cache exceeded the 8 GiB bundle limit or a shared store raised on `put`. It now starts and serves weights. Its `compile_cache` D2D reply is a `miss`, which targets already handle by compiling locally.
- **No shared store.** A source daemon without `--warmup-cache-stores` can never publish a bundle. It no longer scans and SHA-256-hashes its compiled cache roots at startup, so their size can't affect it.
- **Unchanged.** Store configuration and initialization errors, such as an invalid `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`, are still startup errors.

## Validation

Commit 819d052ba6, based on `upstream/main` 11aa1369e2, run on 1x B300. The e2e test runs with `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1`, like the L4 step. No model output changes, so no evals.

New and changed tests with the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_compile_cache_resolve_without_stores_is_a_miss \
    tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_compile_cache_publish_failure_is_a_miss -v
test_compile_cache_resolve_without_stores_is_a_miss PASSED
test_compile_cache_publish_failure_is_a_miss[oversized] PASSED
test_compile_cache_publish_failure_is_a_miss[put] PASSED
3 passed in 2.43s

$ cd tests && VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1 pytest -v -s \
    model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_preload_survives_oversized_compile_cache
test_preload_survives_oversized_compile_cache PASSED
84.68s call     test_preload_survives_oversized_compile_cache
1 passed, 1 warning in 86.11s (0:01:26)
```

The same tests with only `compiled.py` reverted to 11aa1369e2:

```text
E   ValueError: compiled cache is too large      # ..._without_stores_is_a_miss
E   ValueError: compiled cache is too large      # ..._publish_failure_is_a_miss[oversized]
E   NotADirectoryError: [Errno 20] Not a directory: '.../store/<bundle-sha256>'
                                                 # ..._publish_failure_is_a_miss[put]
3 failed in 2.76s

$ cd tests && VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1 pytest -v -s \
    model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_preload_survives_oversized_compile_cache
E   AssertionError: vllm preload exited before ready: ...
      File ".../weight_cache/daemon.py", line 690, in _run_daemon
        daemon.warmup()
      File ".../warmup_cache/compiled.py", line 87, in warmup
        self.prepare()
      File ".../warmup_cache/common.py", line 60, in _manifest
        raise ValueError("compiled cache is too large")
E   ValueError: compiled cache is too large
28.07s call     test_preload_survives_oversized_compile_cache
1 failed, 1 warning in 29.53s
```

Existing compile-cache tests (`pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k "compile_cache and not oversized_compile_cache"`): 10 passed in 6.56s.

CI coverage:
- The e2e test runs in the L4 "Distributed Preload" step. That step's marker expression now also selects `distributed(num_gpus=1)`, and this is the only test in the file with that marker. It needs no Mooncake, so the B200 Mooncake step is unchanged. The step's AMD MI355 mirror inherits the command; I couldn't run it on ROCm.
- The CPU unit tests run in the Model Executor step like the existing compile-cache tests. That step is currently disabled on NVIDIA, so they run on AMD MI300.

## Details

**Root cause.** `CompileArtifactWarmupCache.prepare()` runs from `warmup()` when the daemon listens for D2D peers. It called `_manifest()` before checking for stores, and nothing caught its errors:
- `_manifest()` raises `ValueError("compiled cache is too large")` once the roots exceed `BUNDLE_LIMIT`.
- `_run_daemon` calls `daemon.warmup()` without handling exceptions, so the error stopped the daemon before it served any engine.
- Failures in `_bundle()` (a file changing while it is bundled) and in `store.put()` went the same way.

**Fix.**
- `prepare()` returns before scanning when no store is configured.
- The manifest, bundle and `put` calls run inside a `try`. On failure it logs a warning and leaves `_payload` unset. `resolve()` then returns `None`, and the transport replies `miss`, which is the target's existing fallback.
- `store_sources` is resolved outside the `try`, so store misconfiguration still fails fast, like `FlashInferWarmupCache`.
- `docs/features/preload.md` documents the new behavior in the compiled-cache reuse section.

**Trade-offs and scope.**
- Catching `Exception` means an unexpected bug in this path also only produces a warning. This matches the target-side `adopt_before_load`, which treats any install error the same way, and the bundle is optional.
- `FlashInferWarmupCache._publish_autotune_table` still lets a raising `store.put` propagate. Mooncake's `put` only logs a warning on a nonzero return code, so only native exceptions take that path. I left it unchanged to keep this fix scoped.

**Test notes.**
- The e2e test runs a source daemon without a shared store, so it needs neither Mooncake nor B200. The store-configured failures are covered by the CPU tests, which register a real `DiskArtifactStore` as the shared backend. Their `put` failure is a real `NotADirectoryError` from a store root that is a regular file, not a patched method.
- The e2e test sets `gpu_memory_utilization=0.3`, like the other L4 cases. `request_memory` still applies that setting when `kv_cache_memory_bytes` is set, and the default 0.9 would leave only about 1.7 GiB of headroom on an L4 next to the daemon.
- The oversized cache is a sparse file, and `_manifest()` rejects it from `stat` sizes before hashing anything. The tests never read or write 8 GiB.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/warmup_cache/`. The open PRs that edit `docs/features/preload.md` don't touch the compiled-cache reuse section.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to write the fix and tests and to run the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Reasoning] Return unfinished K2 Horizon reasoning as reasoning
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When K2 Horizon output has no end-of-thinking token and no tool calls (for example cut off by `max_tokens`), non-streaming returns the thinking text as `content`, while streaming returns it as `reasoning`. This PR makes non-streaming return it as `reasoning`, like streaming and like `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser`.

## Claims

- A K2 Horizon response cut off during thinking now has the text in `reasoning` and `content: null`, in both streaming and non-streaming mode.
- Outputs with `</ifm|think>` (or the `medium`/`low` end tokens) or with `<ifm|tool_calls>` parse exactly as before.

## Validation

New unit test `test_unfinished_reasoning_matches_streaming` runs the same output through both modes and checks they agree.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py
python -m pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Before (test only) | `1 failed, 15 passed`: `assert ('', 'still planning') == ('still planning', None)` |
| After | `16 passed`; with the K2 Horizon tool parser tests, `42 passed` |

End-to-end check with K2 Horizon, `--reasoning-parser k2_horizon`, a prompt that needs long thinking and a small `max_tokens` (for example 64):

Parser check with the real K2 Horizon tokenizer (`tokenizer.json` from `IFM/K2-Horizon-7B`, 250,624 tokens including `<ifm|think>` and `</ifm|think>`). The output stops before `</ifm|think>`, as it does when `max_tokens` runs out, and goes through `run_reasoning_extraction`, streamed one decoded token at a time:

Output: `<ifm|think>Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi`

| Mode | `main` (`reasoning` / `content`) | This PR (`reasoning` / `content`) |
|---|---|---|
| non-streaming | `""` / `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` | `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` / `null` |
| streaming | `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` / `null` | `"Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"` / `null` |

On `main` the same truncated output lands in `content` or in `reasoning` depending only on whether the client streams. With this PR both modes agree.

Not run end to end on a GPU yet. The check above uses the model's real tokenizer and special tokens, and the parser has no other inputs on this path.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
    from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
    from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
    from vllm.reasoning import ReasoningParserManager
    from tests.reasoning.utils import run_reasoning_extraction

    tok = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_file=hf_hub_download("IFM/K2-Horizon-7B", "tokenizer.json"))
    req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="IFM/K2-Horizon-7B", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Plan a trip to Hanoi"}], max_tokens=12)
    out = "<ifm|think>Let me plan the trip. First, check the weather in Hanoi"
    pieces = [tok.decode([i]) for i in tok.encode(out, add_special_tokens=False)]
    for streaming in (False, True):
        parser = ReasoningParserManager.get_reasoning_parser("k2_horizon")(tok)
        print(streaming, run_reasoning_extraction(parser, pieces, req, streaming=streaming))

</details>

## Details

Root cause: the last line of `_split_model_output` was `return "", output or None`. The streaming path in the same class buffers that text as reasoning, `extract_content_ids` returns no content ids, and there is no streaming fallback that moves it to content. K2 Horizon has no "thinking off" effort (`reasoning_effort` must be `high`, `medium` or `low`), so text before any boundary is always thinking. The line is now `return output, None`.

Not a duplicate: I searched PRs for "k2 horizon" and open PRs for unfinished or non-streaming reasoning. #59627 changes how the implicit reasoning end reaches structured output and does not touch this function. #57768 adds regex timeouts to the K2 Horizon tool parser. The other open PRs about truncated reasoning are for Kimi K3. No issue reports this bug.

Co-author: Claude.

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Support ModelOpt INT8 pre-processed weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add Fast Start pre-processed weight support for ModelOpt `INT8_PB_WO` linear layers when the selected WNA16 backend is Marlin. This closes the cache-restart gap left by #65272 and advances #56049.

cc: @Isotr0py 

## Claims

- Reuse daemon-exported Marlin-repacked INT8 weights and group scales across CUDA IPC engine restarts.
- Restrict the capability to Marlin with FP16/BF16 activations; Humming, other WNA16 backends, and INT8 MoE remain rejected.
- Recreate Marlin's empty symmetric zero-point runtime handle before processed tensors are attached, so the cached tensor manifest has a matching destination in the meta model.

## Validation

- Added a focused unit test for the capability predicate and restoration of the Marlin zero-point handle on the pre-processed path.
- Ran the pre-commit checks for the changed Python, test, and documentation files.
- Validated a ModelOpt-compatible Qwen2.5-1.5B `INT8_PB_WO` checkpoint with a CUDA vLLM build: ordinary Marlin serving reached HTTP readiness and generated a deterministic response.
- Validated the Fast Start flow end to end: `vllm preload` completed, a second engine attached through `ipc_cache` in zero-copy mode, and the IPC-served request matched the ordinary serving result.

The end-to-end checkpoint used for validation was generated with the declared ModelOpt `INT8_PB_WO` layout. The validation covers the supported Marlin/FP16-BF16 path; it does not claim support for other ModelOpt formats or WNA16 backends.

## Details

`ModelOptLinearMethod` already selects the mixed-precision kernel for `INT8_PB_WO`, while its pre-processed capability only covered FP4, FP8, and MXFP8. The normal Marlin post-load hook repacks the INT8 weight and scales and creates an empty `w_zp`; repeating it on daemon tensors would corrupt the layout. The change registers the empty runtime parameter during model construction, opts in only for the Marlin/FP16/BF16 combination, and skips the second repack while selecting `w_zp` for application. The preload guide documents the supported backend and exclusions.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Fuse the gfx942 mHC seam in the V4.1 AMD model
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

On gfx942, the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD model runs the delayed mHC seam (post, collapse, next pre) as one AITER call, [aiter #6171](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6171) `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed`, instead of several AITER and Triton launches. It takes the call at both seams and the KV write in every step of at least 64 tokens: every step with a prefill chunk of 64 tokens or more, and decode-only steps from 11 concurrent requests with DSpark or 64 without speculative decoding. The dispatch is in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mhc.py`, per [#42770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42770). The shared mHC code is unchanged.

On 4× MI325X, TP4, with and without DSpark:

- 2–5% more output throughput
- 3–12% lower mean TTFT
- up to 4% lower mean TPOT, mostly because requests that are decoding spend most of their time in steps that carry a prefill chunk
- GSM8K and GPQA-Diamond within noise of main

## What changed

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mhc.py`: `supports_mhc_seam` and `mhc_pre_delayed_seam` (same signature as `MHCPreDelayedOp`). There is no vLLM custom op: AITER registers `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed` as a torch op with its own fake, and DSv4.1 isn't torch.compiled. There is no separate warmup either: vLLM's eager profile run, and the eager forward before each graph capture, load the AITER module before any graph uses it.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`: builds the seam when supported, logs it once, and uses it at both seams and the KV write wherever the gfx950 overlap stream and MXFP8 seam ([#67906](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67906)) aren't taken.
- `tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`: new `test_deepseek_v41_gfx942_*` tests: 63 tokens stay on `MHCPreDelayedOp`, 64 calls the op; the KV write takes the op at 64 when the MXFP8 seam is off; graph replay matches eager bitwise; Engram and packed-`fn` (Mega-MHC) seams never call it. The three hand-built decoders set `mhc_seam = None`.
- `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`: adds ":amd: (MI300) mHC Kernels", the MI300 copy of the optional MI355 step (`pytest kernels/mhc`), so the shared mHC tests and these run on CDNA 3. On MI325X: 123 passed, 339 skipped, 0 failed.

## Gating

No flag or environment variable. The model takes the seam when all of these hold:

- the GPU is CDNA 3 and AITER's `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_asm_supported(hidden_size, hc_mult)` accepts the shape (`hc_mult` 4, `hidden_size` 5120);
- the gfx950 RMSNorm seam is off, and neither the gfx950 overlap stream nor the gfx950 MXFP8 seam is taken there (both come first);
- the step has at least 64 tokens, the seam has a post block, and it isn't layer 0.

Shorter steps, layer 0, and Engram stay on `MHCPreDelayedOp`. For shorter steps on gfx942 that is AITER's unfused delayed path, four launches: the pre GEMM with the post folded in, the gates, a Triton pre gate and a Triton collapse. The op is two launches from 64 tokens: AITER's persistent seam kernel, then its asm gates kernel. The server logs `mhc_seam: aiter mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed from 64 tokens` once at startup.

A step with a prefill chunk of 64 tokens or more always takes the op; a lone shorter prompt stays below. Decode-only steps reach it from 11 concurrent requests with DSpark (1 + 5 tokens each) and from 64 without speculative decoding (with `--monokernel`, mono decode takes decode-only steps of up to 42 tokens before they reach the seam, and the gate counts tokens only). 64 is not a tuned crossover: with DSpark, thresholds of 32, 64 and 128 measure the same within noise (sweep below).

## Depends on

[aiter #6171](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6171), included in AITER `v0.1.29`, which main already pins ([#66596](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66596)).

## Performance

4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, language model only, `--monokernel`, prefix cache off, chunked prefill 16384, `vllm bench serve` on random data. Base is vLLM nightly `0.34.0rc1.dev142+g96710245e` with AITER `0.1.28.post1`, whose `aiter/ops/mhc.py` and gfx942 `mhc_seam` kernels are byte-identical to `v0.1.29`, the version main pins. Off is the nightly; on adds this PR. DSpark uses 5 draft tokens with synthetic acceptance (length 4.5 on both arms). These runs used earlier revisions; later commits only moved and renamed code, dropped the vLLM wrapper around the same AITER call, and rebased onto #67906.

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Off | 8192→128 | 1 | **+2.2%** | **−4.8%** | **−1.2%** |
| Off | 8192→128 | 16 | **+3.9%** | **−9.1%** | **−0.5%** |

Prefill-chunk steps take the op and are 4–9% faster, which lowers TTFT. TPOT drops too, because a decoding request spends most of its time in those steps: at 65536→128 conc 4, about 5.5 of them at ~337 ms, against ~122 decode-only steps at ~5.4 ms. Decode-only steps are about 2% faster at conc 16 with DSpark.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Add HY4
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add the recipe for [tencent/Hy4](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4), released today, at `recipes/models/tencent/Hy4.yaml`. The model card links to `recipes.vllm.ai/tencent/Hy4`, which does not exist yet. Model support landed in #68296; this PR is recipe-only.

## Claims

- The default command reproduces the model card's launch line: `tencent/Hy4-FP8`, TP8, Rust frontend, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, BF16 compute, paired `hy_v4` tool and reasoning parsers, DFly2 with five speculative tokens, one image per prompt.
- A BF16 variant (`tencent/Hy4`) is offered alongside the FP8 default.
- Install: the official `vllm/vllm-openai:hy4` image first, nightly wheel second (`min_vllm_version: 0.35.0`, `nightly_required`).
- Single-node TP only, because DFly2 requires DP = PP = PCP = DCP = 1. AMD Instinct is marked unsupported.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir ~/vllm/recipes` from vllm-project/recipes@main (the `Recipes` PR check): `✓ vllm recipes from … are valid against the renderer`.
- `node scripts/build-recipes-api.mjs`: `✓ JSON API: 234 models`. The rendered default for 8x B300:

  ```text
  docker run --gpus all \
    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    -e VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
    vllm/vllm-openai:hy4 tencent/Hy4-FP8 \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --max-model-len 131072 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dfly"}'
  ```

- `pre-commit run --files recipes/models/tencent/Hy4.yaml` passed.
- Checked against sources:
  - `tencent/Hy4` and `tencent/Hy4-FP8` are public; both configs are `HYV4VLForConditionalGeneration` with `max_position_embeddings` 1,048,576 and `num_nextn_predict_layers` 0.
  - `vllm/vllm-openai:hy4` exists on Docker Hub (amd64 and arm64). There is no `vllm-openai-rocm:hy4`.
  - `registry.py` has `HYV4VLForConditionalGeneration` on main and not at `v0.34.0`. Today's cu130 nightly wheel (`gc3310a889`) contains #68296.
  - VRAM hints are checkpoint bytes × 1.2: 786.3 GB → 944 (FP8), 1,548.9 GB → 1859 (BF16).
- No server was launched for this PR. Earlier evaluations ran on 8x B300 at TP8 with commit `428c371`, the Python frontend and DFly2 off, on pre-release snapshots. The recipe claims no `verified` hardware.

## Details

- **Limits.** `--max-model-len 131072`, `--max-num-seqs 32` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` are the evaluated settings. The model card sets none of them; the guide says so and tells readers to raise them.
- **Defaults vs evidence.** The defaults follow the model card, so the Rust frontend, tool calling and DFly2 are on by default although the evaluations above ran without them. Happy to make them opt-in if reviewers prefer the evaluated path as the default.
- **AMD.** `vllm/models/hy_v4/amd/` has the text backbone only (no vision encoder, no DFly drafter), and the recipe passes a CUDA attention backend.
- **Not a duplicate.** No open or merged PR adds `recipes/models/tencent/Hy4.yaml`; #68295 added HY4 Flash, and #68839 is HY4 Flash on ROCm.
