commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Clean up the specialized decode test primitives (follow-up to #67135)
commits.pr_body:
Review follow-ups to #67135 (merged), which added the float64 reference and the specialized decode format primitives. All of it is in `tests/`, and there is no behaviour change: the same 10 test ids, the same inputs, the same bit-exact assertions. Opened separately rather than folded into the next PR so the cleanup is reviewable on its own.

Stacked under #67977 (PR 4), which will rebase on this.

## The split

`tests/models/common/specialized_decode/primitives.py` held two unrelated things: a FlyDSL test-kernel builder, and a set of plain-torch input generators. It becomes two files, split by what the code does rather than by what it is written in:

| file | what is in it |
|---|---|
| `harness.py` | the only file that needs FlyDSL: builds the map kernel that calls a model's device helper on every lane |
| `inputs.py` | plain torch: the generators that make a rounding rule observable, and the comparison of what comes back |
| `reference.py` | unchanged except for its docstring: the float64 definitions |

A model whose helpers are not FlyDSL device functions a test kernel can call cannot use `harness.py`, but can still use the other two.

## Raised in review of #67135

- `full()` was dead, removed.
- `gen()` and `log_uniform()` are building blocks of the generators next to them, now `_gen` and `_log_uniform`.
- Type hints throughout. `primitives.py` had 23 of 25 names untyped and the dsv41 test 14 of 14; `harness.py`, `inputs.py` and the test are now fully typed and clean under the repo's mypy settings.
- `assert_equal` is now `assert_bit_exact`, and its docstring says why a bare `torch.equal` is not enough where it is used: the generators run to ~2^20 rows and a bare `False` over a million roundings says nothing about which one broke. The handful-of-values cases still use `torch.equal` directly.
- `HelperSet` / `own_helper` / `params` are gone; see below.
- `reference.py`'s docstring is shorter, and says how a model other than dsv41 would use the file.

## Found while going back over it

- `_map_kernel` was `@cache`d on a key holding `fn`, which is a fresh closure at every call site, so the cache could never hit. Removed, with a docstring saying why. FlyDSL's own cache, keyed on the kernel name and the sources digest, is what actually stops a recompile.
- `run(..., sources=...)` made every caller pass `sources=H.sources_digest(_PKG)`; forgetting it would silently test against a stale compiled helper. `run` now takes `package=` and computes the digest itself.
- `run` asserts its columns have equal row counts instead of silently truncating, and `assert_bit_exact` asserts the two shapes match before comparing (otherwise `!=` broadcasts a mismatch into a square of comparisons and the report is about rows nothing computed).
- `DEV` was hardcoded `"cuda"`, now `current_platform.device_type`.
- Every skip gate now comes before the imports it would make pointless, so a non-MI3xx ROCm box stops before importing the model's FlyDSL device modules rather than after.
- NaN is zeroed out of the bf16 inputs. That was undocumented and looked like a dodge; it is now commented as deliberate, since what a NaN payload becomes under a truncation to 7 mantissa bits is the ISA's business and float64 has no definition to check it against.
- The scale code sweep runs 1..253 and skips 0, 254 and 255. Also undocumented, and the reason turned out to be worth writing down: those are the codes where the bit tricks `code << 23` and `(254 - code) << 23` part company with the E8M0 definition (`pow2(0)` and `rcp_pow2(254)` are `+0.0` where the code names 2^-127; 255 is an infinity for both), which is why `common/mx.py` documents them over `[1, 253]`. Nothing in the model reaches them: both are fed `code_ceil(amax / FP8_MAX)` or `mx_code(amax)`, and dividing a finite float32 by 224 caps the code at 248. Worth a separate look, though, that `code_ceil` clamps to `[1, 254]` while `rcp_pow2` is only exact to 253; it is the divisor rather than either helper that keeps them apart.
- `test_scale_index` is the one helper here that runs on the host rather than through a kernel. Now stated in the docstring rather than left to be noticed.
- The `FP8_MAX` lookup went through `HelperSet.find`, which returns `None` if the name moves; it is a plain module attribute now, so a move is an `ImportError`.

## The one judgement call: dropping `HelperSet`

The dsv41 test used to resolve helpers by name at runtime over a tuple of module paths, and `own_helper` returned `None` where a module had only imported a name rather than defined it. I replaced that with explicit imports and small tables.

The reason the reflection existed is real: the model carries two copies of these helpers, and although `attention/device.py` does take `GFX942` and three helpers from `common/gfx942.py`, every helper in these tables it defines again for itself. The tables now say outright which copy carries what, which the reflection hid. I checked every helper the test touches against both copies first, so the parametrisation is provably the same, and confirmed it by collecting both versions side by side: the 10 ids are identical.

The trade is that a renamed helper is now an `ImportError` instead of a silently skipped parameter. The other half of that trade is that `own_helper` also guarded against the two copies quietly collapsing into one, so the test now asserts at import that they are still two distinct functions.

The duplication itself belongs in `vllm/models/`, not here: roughly 40 top-level names are duplicated across the mono package, and `mx_code` (attention) and `vllm_mx_code` (MoE) are the same rule under two names. I will file that separately; when it lands, these tables collapse to one column.

## Test plan

On MI355X (gfx950), against the merged tree, with the command the Buildkite steps run:

```
pytest -v -s tests/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono/test_primitives.py
10 passed in 7.8s   (17s wall, including interpreter start and the vllm/aiter imports)
```

Unchanged from before this PR: same 10 tests, same inputs, so no extra CI load. The two steps that listed `primitives.py` now list `harness.py` and `inputs.py`; no step gains or loses a test.

Also checked:

- `--collect-only` gives 10 ids, byte-identical to main's.
- Mutation checked: perturbing `R.bf16_rne` and `R.mx_code_vllm` fails the corresponding test with a message naming the helper and the offending inputs, so the assertions still bite after the refactor.
- `pre-commit` clean on the changed files (mypy's only failure is the pre-existing 3.10 syntax error in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/.../attn_fi.py`).
- The gfx950 arm only; the gfx942 arm (FNUZ, fmax 224) is covered by the MI300 Buildkite step.

Part of #68016 (T1).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Transformers backend] Fuse packed qkv that is sliced, not split
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix `Phi3ForCausalLM` (Phi-3, Phi-3.5-mini, Phi-4-mini, Phi-4, Phi-4-reasoning) failing at `tensor_parallel_size > 1` on the Transformers backend since #66559, by teaching `PackedQKVFuser` to fuse a packed `qkv_proj` that is sliced rather than split.

## Claims

- `Phi3ForCausalLM` at TP2 no longer crashes in `Attention.forward`; GSM8K at TP2 matches TP1 and the #66559 reference on Phi-3-mini-4k, Phi-3.5-mini, Phi-4-mini, Phi-4 and Phi-4-reasoning.
- TP1 is unchanged in accuracy (the fused projection is now a `QKVParallelLinear` there too).
- `split`-based packed-QKV modules take exactly the same path as before.

## Validation

Evals ran on `91ea0b40c2` (base: `ecc827ebbf`, #67833), transformers 5.22.0. The implementation was then reworked in `5130e5f5d9`..`dd66a8524c` (see Details); the unit tests below and the re-run below are from the current head `7eefbe19e9`. `test_distributed[Phi-4-mini]` runs in CI.

**Re-run on `7eefbe19e9`** (`microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct`, bf16, TP2, B200, full GSM8K 5-shot, same commands as below): 0.739 (0.001 invalid), vs 0.741 on the original implementation; `Fused: qkv_proj (self_attn: Phi3Attention) -> QKVParallelLinear` logged.

**Unit tests**

```
$ pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_linear.py -q -k "qkv or sliced"
26 passed, 1 skipped, 39 deselected, 14 warnings in 3.81s
```

New tests (7: 3 detection and numerics, 1 per-rank slicing at TP2, 3 negative cases); the positive ones fail on the base fuser and pass with the fix:

```
$ pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_linear.py -q -k sliced     # base packed_qkv.py
FAILED test_linear.py::test_detects_and_rewrites_sliced_qkv[SlicedQKVAttention]
FAILED test_linear.py::test_detects_and_rewrites_sliced_qkv[RopeSlicedQKVAttention]
FAILED test_linear.py::test_detects_and_rewrites_sliced_qkv[AnnotatedSlicedQKVAttention]
FAILED test_linear.py::test_sliced_qkv_forward_reads_per_rank_sections
4 failed, 3 passed, 59 deselected in 1.01s

$ pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_linear.py -q -k sliced     # with this PR
7 passed, 59 deselected in 0.98s
```

**End to end** (`microsoft/phi-4`, bf16, 300-question subset)

```bash
vllm serve microsoft/phi-4 -tp $TP --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --port 8123
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8123 --num-questions 300 --max-concurrency 32
```

| Code | TP | Result | `Fused: qkv_proj` logged |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (`ecc827ebbf`) | 2 | server fails at startup | no |
| main | 1 | 0.910 (0 invalid) | no |
| this PR | 1 | 0.913 (1 invalid) | yes |
| this PR | 2 | 0.920 (0 invalid) | yes |

300 questions is about ±1.6 points standard error; single runs.

<details>
<summary>Failure on main (TP2), raw error</summary>

```
torch._dynamo.exc.ObservedRuntimeError: raised exception RuntimeError("Dynamo failed to run FX node with fake tensors: call_method view(*(FakeTensor(..., size=(s27, 1280), dtype=torch.bfloat16), -1, 5, 128), **{}): got ValueError('Cannot view a tensor with shape torch.Size([s27, 1280]) and strides (7680, 1) as a tensor with shape (2*s27, 5, 128)!')")
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py", line 581, in forward
    value = value.view(-1, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_size_v)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Models from #66559 at TP2, full GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions)</summary>

```bash
vllm serve $MODEL -tp 2 --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len $LEN --port 8123
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8123 --max-concurrency 32
```

| Model | `--max-model-len` | This PR, TP2 | #66559 reference | Invalid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` | 4096 | 0.784 | 0.779 | 0.007 |
| `microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct` | 8192 | 0.700 | 0.697 | 0.002 |
| `microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct` | 8192 | 0.741 | 0.741 | 0.001 |

`microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning`: TP2 serves and answers correctly; 200-question GSM8K subset is 0.940 at TP2 and 0.925 at TP1.

</details>

Not run: quantized Phi-3 checkpoints, and Phi-4-multimodal / Phi-4-reasoning-vision with real weights (the fuser matches `Phi4MultimodalAttention` in a unit-level check).

## Details

**Root cause.** HF's `Phi3Attention` cuts the fused projection with global offsets (`qkv[..., :query_pos]`, `qkv[..., query_pos:query_pos + kv]`, `qkv[..., query_pos + kv:]`) rather than calling `.split(...)`. `PackedQKVFuser` only matched `.split((q, kv, kv))`, so `qkv_proj` was left unfused and took HF's TP plan, `colwise_gather_output` ("replicate due to the slicing of qkv"). Every rank then held the full 40/10/10 heads, while vLLM's `Attention` is built for per-rank heads (20/5/5 at TP2), which fails at the `view` above.

**Change** (`fusers/packed_qkv.py`).
- `match`: one pass over the graph tries each node as `.split((q, kv, kv))` (`_split_sizes`, renamed from `_packed_sizes`), then as a linear whose output has exactly three direct users `x[..., :q]`, `x[..., q:k_end]`, `x[..., k_end:]` with int bounds (`_sliced_sizes`). Both forms share the linear and `q + 2 * kv == out_features` checks. Matching on direct users (not `upstream_linear`) keeps rotary-style slices of derived tensors from matching.
- `update_forward`: `_rewrite_split` rewrites the split sizes to the per-rank widths, as before. `_rewrite_slices` rewrites the three slice bounds in place to the per-rank offsets (`output_sizes[i] // tp_size`), so `qkv` stays a tensor. Each returns whether it applied; if neither did, `update_forward` raises and the module stays unfused.

**Tests** (`test_backend.py`). `check_implementation` now takes `num_fused` as a dict of fuser class name to count per layer, read from `model.fusers`, so the Phi-4-mini case asserts `PackedQKVFuser` rather than any `QKVParallelLinear`.

**Scope and limits.**
- Only `phi3` and `phi4_multimodal` in the installed transformers slice three ways off a linear's output; the mixers checked (`Mamba2Mixer`, `MambaMixer`, `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet`) are not matched.
- Like the existing `split` form, nothing checks that the slices feed attention; a module with an unrelated three-way head-aligned tiling of a linear output would match.
- `Phi3MLP`'s `gate_up_proj` (chunked) stays on HF's gather plan: correct, but with an extra all-gather per MLP. Fusing it would be a separate change.
- TP sizes that do not divide the KV head count (e.g. TP4 with 10 KV heads) still fail, as with the previous native implementation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Skip GPU restores for cancelled KV imports
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip HiSparse host-to-device restores when an external KV receive completes after its request has been cancelled. A successful receive can still publish the completed host prefix.

## Details

Cancellation removes the request from the HiSparse connector's live-request map. Its landing blocks stay allocated until the outstanding receive completes. Previously, a successful receive acknowledgment caused the coordinator to schedule the tail restore and promote eligible historical pages even after the request had been removed. Those transfers pinned GPU blocks until another worker acknowledgment, although the request could no longer consume the restored KV.

At receive completion, use the connector's existing live-request map to decide whether to schedule restores. For a cancelled request, advance the GPU-copy indexing cursor past the imported prefix. This lets host prefix publication proceed without advertising a GPU landing block that the worker never filled. If a restore was already submitted before cancellation, its endpoints remain pinned until the worker acknowledges completion.

## Claims

A CPU reproduction using the scheduler, MultiConnector and three HiSparse resident groups produced the following results on successful receive completion.

| Request state at receive completion | Base | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Live request, restores queued | 4 | 4 |
| Cancelled request, restores queued | 4 | 0 |
| Cancelled request, GPU block references held by these restores | 12 | 0 |

Both fixes can land independently. [#68726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68726) limits how much spare GPU capacity a live request may use for historical pages. This change addresses a late receive acknowledgment for a finished request.

## Validation

Tested `7cb3abfbdb92258d8f463021fc6ffd8e73b8ac4d` against `2a55c28737f5ef7f6839509649d023d8a6151b75`. The updated receive-completion test on the base reported `1 failed, 3 passed in 2.12s`: cancellation followed by a successful receive queued two unexpected restores. The regression exercises both successful and failed receives, host prefix publication and GPU-copy eligibility. The abort-after-submission test checks the reference counts before and after the worker acknowledgment.

```sh
pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_host_receive_completion_without_spill_metadata tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_hisparse_aborted_promotion_keeps_pages_until_restored
# 5 passed in 2.10s

pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py
# 261 passed, 2 xfailed in 55.64s
```

Validation covered CPU scheduling, the allocator and connector behavior. The MultiConnector reproduction used scripted worker acknowledgments. End-to-end GPU transport and model evaluation were outside this run. AI assistance was used to develop the patch, tests and description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][FA4] Cover paged dense prefill specializations in the warmup
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR closes two FA4 warmup gaps that leave real prefill shapes to compile during serving. The dense FA4 warmup now covers the paged prefill specializations of every model family, and it sizes its synthetic page table so that a cache page larger than the warmup length warms the same specialization that serving uses. It started in #62800, which keeps the KV cache page fixes. The two PRs share no files and don't depend on each other, so either can land first. It is also independent of #62961, #62962, #62963 and #62964.

## Claims

- FA4 warmup covers the dense paged prefill specializations (packed-query staging, persistent and non-persistent, SplitKV, and the varlen batch lookup when `max_num_seqs` exceeds FA4's `BIN_BATCH_SEARCH_THRESH`) for every model family, and each warmup key compiles a distinct kernel. The existing specialized hd256 and SM90 hd512 paths stay as they are.
- The warmup sizes its synthetic page table with ceiling division. A cache page larger than the warmup length otherwise warms a broadcast (zero-stride) specialization that serving never uses.

## Validation

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed below.

The new test is a native compilation-cache test. It fails when a served shape misses the warmup or when two warmup keys compile the same kernel. I broke the page-table fix on purpose to check that the test catches it, and reverting it fails the 4 large-page cases of the 8 native tests on B300. Letting SplitKV keys claim static persistence fails all 8 on the duplicate-kernel check.

On CPU (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, one pytest process per file), the 8 native tests in `test_flash_attn_warmup.py` skip without CUDA. Across 21 attention, KV-cache, spec-decode and worker test files, this PR passes 735 tests, the same as `main` (`537a79f0fc`). The 77 failures are the same pre-existing cases on both builds: 62 tests that need Hugging Face model configs the offline runner lacks, 8 CPU-builder cases in `test_group_head_counts.py` and 7 in `test_gpu_model_runner.py`. One more `test_kv_cache_planning.py` test timed out in its subprocess during the parallel run on this PR, and it passes on both builds when run alone. `pre-commit` passes on the range.

On B300, `test_flash_attn_warmup.py` passes natively (8 passed). A CUDA probe ran real paged attention after the warmup over 102 served shapes (batches of 1, 16 and 300, query lengths from 1 to 1611, full and sliding-window layers, automatic SplitKV). It had 0 forward compilation misses against 14 on `main`, and its outputs matched `main` bit for bit. The warmup compiles 5 forward kernels from 5 keys with `max_num_seqs=256` and 8 from 8 with `max_num_seqs=1024`, and the hd256 warmup compiles the same native kernels as on `main`. A TP4 hybrid Mamba2 model with a 9728-token page served 8 requests with 0 runtime forward misses and 0 inference-time JIT warnings. I measured the Mamba2 run on the previous base (`56e67b46a3`) before the warmup key change, where the first two commits sat together with the KV cache fixes that are now #62800.

```bash
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_warmup.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flash_attn_warmup.py   # on B300
```

## Not a duplicate

I ran the duplicate-work searches from `AGENTS.md` §1 (open PRs, with keywords on FA4 warmup, `FA4DenseAttentionKernel` and warmup page tables). They found related work, and none of it makes the same fix. This PR uses no code from them.

- #48156 (dense FA4 warmup) predates the in-tree `FA4DenseAttentionKernel` warmup framework from #55768. This PR extends that framework.
- #61221 adds the persistent variant to Kimi-K3's vision FA4 warmup, which is a separate warmup provider. This PR covers the dense paged attention provider.

## Includes and credits

This PR contains no code from other open PRs.

## Details

- The changes touch only the warmup provider. Runtime attention dispatch and arithmetic are unchanged, and so are the existing specialized hd256 and SM90 hd512 warmup paths. Warming every model family trades startup time for no forward-kernel compilation during serving. SplitKV's combine and scheduling kernels still compile on first use (3 compilations across the 102 probe shapes). On B300 the dense warmup compiles in 8 to 13 s per attention spec. Qwen3.8-27B selects FlashInfer by default on B300, so its server start does not include this cost, and the startup cost on a full FA4 model is still to be measured.
- All GPU measurements are on B300.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Fix missing SwiGLU clamp in batched DeepGEMM
commits.pr_body:
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base sets `swiglu_limit=10`. Batched DeepGEMM omitted this limit in its fused SwiGLU and FP8 quantization step. With `deepep_low_latency` on 8×H200, the original code produced 9 severe token log-probability mismatches in 16,384 tokens. One token had logprob −0.31 versus −31.68 from the reference.

Apply the model's optional limit before SiLU and multiplication. Cap the gate at the upper bound and clamp the up projection to ±limit. The CUDA implementation specializes on the presence of the limit at host dispatch. The Triton kernel takes the limit as a compile-time constant. The default is `None`.

**Performance with clamp disabled.** The CUDA grid, thread count, prefetch depth, shared memory allocation and stream match upstream `ca04fba321`. All six native CUDA variants emitted byte-identical GPU instructions on both SM90 and SM100. All 452 tested unclamped Triton specializations per target also had byte-identical executable sections. SM100 code generation was checked by cross-compilation. On H200, 12 alternating rounds on each of the 25 configurations flagged by the earlier screening gave an across-configuration median of +0.01% and a range of -0.53% to +0.09% versus upstream. These timings measure GPU execution; eager dispatch and end-to-end throughput were not measured for this revision.

**Performance with clamp enabled.** On a 30-case H200 native kernel panel, enabling the required arithmetic changed latency by a median of +2.91% and a maximum of +5.46% compared with the unclamped upstream kernel (three balanced CUPTI rounds, CUDA graphs, cold L2). The panel includes FP8 scale formats, different expert loads and the model's H=2048 widths. The Triton clamp implementation retains its previously measured overhead, including +6.96% on H200 for E128/H7168 with a skewed token distribution. These figures are kernel timings.

**Correctness.** The extension was rebuilt with incremental CMake. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py` passed all 110 tests. Tests compare the fused clamp with independently preclamped BF16 inputs, including zero limits, odd token counts, empty experts and padding. Pre-commit hooks passed.

At `ad9819ea79`, the Base FP8 checkpoint `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base@8855555deef230a27a21a8d6f294b7b7497759b6` ran on 8×H200 with TP1/DP8, expert parallelism, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs and `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`. All eight workers selected `BatchedDeepGemmExperts` in all 43 MoE layers with limit 10. Nine failing prefixes were replayed three times each, with zero severe mismatches. GSM8K (200 examples, five-shot, greedy, seed 1234) scored 188/200 strict and 188/200 flexible. This is a smoke evaluation. The runtime used DeepEP 2.1.0; the original report used 1.2.1.

**Other backends.** The HPC backend independently reproduced the missing clamp on the same model (34 severe mismatches in 32,563 tokens). Models requiring the limit now exclude HPC during backend selection. Explicitly forcing HPC reports the unsupported configuration. The GPU kernel and constructor for HPC retain their existing behavior.

The audit uses the original expert constructors, without the proposed model-only fallback changes. Runtime inspection checks the actual selected expert class and the clamp reaching each of 43 MoE layers in the inspected worker. Negative results mean no reproduction in these workloads, not proof that a backend is universally correct.

| Original backend | Hardware / weights | Fresh tokens / severe mismatches | Comparison |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Ordinary DeepGEMM | H200 / Base FP8 | 32,563 / 0 | Generated vs teacher-forced logprobs |
| Ordinary DeepGEMM FP4 | GB200 / MXFP4 | 32,692 / 0 | Same backend, generated vs prefill |
| FlashInfer CUTLASS | H200 / Base FP8 | 32,563 / 0 | Independent H200 DeepGEMM reference |
| TRT-LLM modular FP8 | GB200 / Base FP8 | 32,563 / 0 | Independent H200 DeepGEMM reference |
| TRT-LLM modular MXFP4 | GB200 / MXFP4 | 32,433 / 0 | Same backend, generated vs prefill |
| CuteDSL NVFP4 | GB200 / NVIDIA NVFP4 | 32,673 / 2 threshold outliers | Same backend, generated vs prefill |
| FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4 | GB200 / same NVIDIA NVFP4 | 32,766 / 1 threshold outlier | Same backend, generated vs prefill |

These deployments already forward limit=10 through the normal quantization configuration; the proposed model-only fallback changes were unnecessary for them and have been removed. The first five rows also replayed the nine original failing prefixes three times without the original severe anomaly. Same-backend prefill checks are not independent accuracy references.

CuteDSL NVFP4 correctly receives limit=10. Its two threshold outliers do not establish a missing-clamp defect: replays vary (one token scored -6.33, -9.19, -13.20), unlike the original deterministic high-confidence anomaly. The removed fallback change would pass exactly the same limit. A same-checkpoint CUTLASS control also has one threshold outlier; scoring the CuteDSL-generated tokens with CUTLASS gives three. **NVFP4 is not a clean numerical pass:** these residual differences remain unlocalized and are not claimed fixed. Neither backend receives a speculative change in this PR.

GB200 runs use TP=1/DP=2/EP on two GPUs, AG/RS communication, max length 8192. MXFP4 checkpoint: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash@60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1`. NVFP4 checkpoint: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4@e3cd60e7de98e9867116860d522499a728de1cf9`.

MoonEP and TRT-LLM MxInt4 have no trained-model end-to-end accuracy result in this audit and receive **no changes**. Source inspection shows MoonEP already rejects quantization-sourced clamp parameters and the normal unquantized method forwards the model limit. TRT-LLM MxInt4 does not advertise DeepSeek-V4 routing support; no suitable checkpoint was available. No ROCm/XPU correctness claim is made.

**Contribution notes.** #64976 addresses standalone SwiGLU strides/ranks and #32735 refactors the masked helper. Neither implements the missing batched MoE clamp. AI assistance was used for diagnosis, implementation, tests and this description. The human submitter must review the diff and run relevant tests before merge.

commits.pr_title: [Kimi K3.1][Specialized decode] Serve GQA DSpark drafts on the specialized drafter
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Builds Kimi-K3.1's GQA sliding-window DSpark draft ([`Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark), a `Qwen3DSparkModel`) on the specialized decode's drafter under `decode_backend=latency_specialized`, as the MLA preview draft (`K3DSparkModel`) already is. On 8x B300 with the real Kimi-K3.1-Pro, the draft step drops from 751 µs to 463 µs (−38%) at TP8 and at TP8 + DCP8.

No open PR covers this (searched "specialized drafter GQA", "Kimi K3.1 DSpark specialized", "Qwen3DSpark specialized decode", "K3.1 DSpark drafter").

## Claims

- With `decode_backend=latency_specialized`, `Qwen3DSparkModel` drafts of Kimi-K3.1 are built as `SpecializedQwen3DSparkForCausalLM`; nothing changes without it.
- Draft step: 751 → 464 µs at TP8, 751 → 463 µs at TP8 + DCP8 (batch 1, k = 4).
- Full decode step at TP8 + DCP8 (the recipe's AgentX preset): 8.39 → 8.12 ms (−3.2%); the target verify (~7.2 ms) is the rest of the step.

## Validation

8x B300, real [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro), the recipe's B300 AgentX TP8 + DCP8 concurrency-1 preset (no host KV offload), `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark` with 4 draft tokens, probabilistic drafting, block rejection:

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 --use-replayssm \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' --max-num-seqs 2 --language-model-only \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,10]}'
```

The stock drafter run is the same command on main (`8700cc9ba0`); TP8 drops the three DCP flags. Step times are from torch profiles (rank 0, 60 steps); throughput from 6 chat prompts at temperature 0, one at a time, `max_tokens=400`.

| Config | Drafter | Draft step | Target verify | Full step | Acceptance length | Output tok/s (1 stream) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 + DCP8 | stock | 751 µs | 7244 µs | 8391 µs | 3.49 | 325.7 |
| TP8 + DCP8 | this PR | 463 µs | 7271 µs | 8123 µs | 3.56 | 330.7 |
| TP8 | stock\* | 751 µs | – | – | – | – |
| TP8 | this PR | 464 µs | 7021 µs | 7844 µs | 3.62 | 350.9 |

\*Stock drafter at TP8 measured with the stock target decode (draft graph time does not depend on the target's decode backend: 751 / 759 µs with the specialized / stock target at TP8 + DCP8).

![Draft step breakdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/mgoin/pr-68701-assets/draft_step_breakdown.png)

![Decode step at TP8 + DCP8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mgoin/vllm/mgoin/pr-68701-assets/decode_step_tp8_dcp8.png)

Where the draft step's GPU time goes (µs per step, kernels summed; they overlap):

| Category | Stock | This PR | What changed |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Layer GEMMs (QKV, o, MLP, context K/V, context projection) | 277 | 164 | `DraftGemm` warp split-K; context projection column-parallel |
| Markov sampling | 146 | 45 | fused, vocab-sharded Markov steps (`markov.py`) |
| Attention, norms, RoPE, KV write | 179 | 129 | eager draft forward (no torch.compile) on the same kernels; FA4 attention unchanged |
| Collectives | 112 | 110 | mailbox gather for the context projection and logits; embedding all-reduce fused with the first RMSNorm |
| LM head | 47 | 47 | the target's low-latency lm_head (unchanged) |

Output text is coherent in every run; acceptance is in line with the recipe's golden 3.19 at 4 tokens. The throughput difference is within the noise of 6 prompts; the step-time difference is the measured claim.

Checks: `pre-commit run --files vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/drafter/gqa.py vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/drafter/model.py` passes (ruff, mypy, docstring style).

No tests are added: CI has no Kimi-K3.1 checkpoint (the specialized decode needs the full 896-expert model and 8 SM100 GPUs), and the new class only composes the existing drafter parts, which `tests/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_specialized_decode_drafter.py` and `test_k31_drafter_comm.py` cover. The validation above is the coverage.

## Details

- `drafter/gqa.py` adds `SpecializedQwen3DSparkForCausalLM` / `SpecializedQwen3DSparkModel`, the GQA counterpart of `SpecializedK3DSparkForCausalLM`, built from the same parts: `linears.DraftGemm` for every drafter linear and the fused context K/V GEMM, `linears.draft_logits`, `markov.sample_sequential`, `comm.DrafterComm` (context-projection and logits gathers, the embedding's `ArNorm`), and `model._gathered_linear` for the column-parallel `fc`.
- The model disables `o_proj` / `down_proj` reductions and reduces them in the following RMSNorm with `fused_allreduce_rms_norm`, which the compiled stock model gets from its fusion pass; it is `@ignore_torch_compile`, like `K3DSparkModel`, since the drafter's custom kernels run in its forward.
- `drafter/model.py:register()`, which `specialized_decode_config` calls under `latency_specialized` on a Kimi-K3 target, now also registers `Qwen3DSparkModel`. It is only called in that process, so other `Qwen3DSparkModel` drafts are unaffected.
- The draft attention stays on the stock FLASH_ATTN sliding-window path (~70 µs of the step); the preview drafter's folded MLA attention does not apply to GQA.

Limitations: the remaining draft time is spread over attention (~129 µs with its norms, RoPE and KV writes), the ten all-reduce + RMSNorm sites (~73 µs) and the context projection (K = 35840 is too wide for the warp split-K, ~16 µs on cuBLAS).

[Kernel][Perf] Run GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 routed experts in SM90 DeepGEMM Mega MoE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Runs GLM-5.3-Flash's block-FP8 routed and shared experts in DeepGEMM Mega MoE on SM90 (`--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on H200), through a new weight format `MEGA_MOE_FP8_BLOCK_SM90`. The checkpoint's E4M3 weights and FP32 128x128 block scales go to the kernel without MXFP8 requantization. SM100 keeps `MEGA_MOE_MXFP8`. Builds on the GLM-5.3-Flash Mega MoE path of #60895.

Pins DeepGEMM to vllm-project/DeepGEMM `dev` [`44cba7d`](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/44cba7d28066182852005c59052f035ebc18e211), the merge of vllm-project/DeepGEMM#57 on top of main's pin.

## Claims

- At default memory on 8x H200, Mega MoE leads both main backends (default and FI MoE-EP) at every measured point, with the largest KV pool: 66.44 GiB per GPU against 60.12 (FI MoE-EP) and 54.05 (main default). On 4x H200 it leads FI MoE-EP and DeepEP v2 at every point; main default ran out of memory there once (Limitations).
- On the AgentX sweep from c=1 to c=256, Mega MoE beats main's default MoE at every level on 4x and 8x H200 in output tok/s per GPU (+12% to +24% at c=1..32), and per user everywhere except c=128 on 4x H200 (-12%, inside the noise). Per-user speed is +26% to +34% at c=1..32.
- Mega MoE leaves more memory for the KV cache at the same memory setting: 3.1-4.4 GiB more per GPU at DP4 (11-16.5% more KV tokens), 6.3-12.4 GiB more at DP8 (10.5-22.9%). This is part of the feature and gives most of the lead over FI MoE-EP at AgentX c=64.
- At an equal 24 GiB KV pool (DP4), AgentX is +12% (c=16) and +16% (c=64) over main's default MoE. Against FI MoE-EP it is +10.5% at c=16 and -2.1% at c=64, where the pool is the limit.
- GSM8K, paired per question, shows no difference to main's default MoE; logprobs are as close to main default as FI MoE-EP's are.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on H200, vLLM default memory (`--gpu-memory-utilization` 0.92) for every arm unless stated, no MTP, no EPLB. One API server per DP rank behind the llm-d prefix-aware router.

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  -dp 4 --data-parallel-size-local 4 --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tokenizer-mode glm5_next --max-model-len 142000 \
  --disable-extensible-kv-cache --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  <arm flag>
```

| Arm | Arm flag |
|---|---|
| Mega MoE (this PR) | `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` |
| FI MoE-EP (#62603) | `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` |
| DeepEP v2 | `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` (DEEPGEMM FP8 experts) |
| main default | none (FLASHINFER_CUTLASS + `allgather_reducescatter`) |

Random: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`, `d` = 1k in / 1k out, `p` = 8k in / 256 out, prompts max(32, 4c), prefix cache reset per point. AgentX: agentic-coding trace replay, 900 s per level. Output tok/s is for the whole server. Single runs unless stated.

The tables were measured on main `f48bfde4d` with this PR's code as of `89f5229e2` and DeepGEMM `a49ea3f`, before the rebase onto `191e5d5df`. Sanity runs of Mega MoE at DP4 default memory on the rebased code matched:

| Metric | measured base | DeepGEMM `b582b99` | DeepGEMM `b3669fe` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| KV pool per engine, max seqs | 31.24 GiB, 657 | same | same |
| GSM8K | 0.9295 | 0.9363 | 0.9303 |
| d c=1 / c=64, out tok/s | 107.48 / 2837.53 | 107.12 / 2853.73 | 107.63 / 2849.02 |
| AgentX c=16, out tok/s | 339.92 | 339.82 | 339.59 |
| server errors | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The GSM8K differences are inside the 1.06 pt spread between two runs of one server.

After the rebase onto main `3d836e13e` and the re-pin to DeepGEMM `44cba7d`, DP4+EP4 on 4x H200 (two interleaved fresh-server runs per arm, mean; text only, `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'` because main now needs it on the Python frontend), output tok/s per GPU:

| p c=16 | 139.7 | 165.8 | +18.7% |
| p c=64 | 225.6 | 286.8 | +27.1% |

GSM8K (first 250 questions) 0.936, server errors 0.

### Blackwell (SM100)

On 8x B300 (main `191e5d5df` + DeepGEMM `196f338` against this PR), unit test results are identical in every file, and the SM100 DeepGEMM SASS is identical for every paired kernel instance (293, including 229 from the E2E servers). On real GLM layers in FP8 and BF16 the routing switch picks the same experts in all 32 cases; CUDA graph replay after layerwise and direct reloads equals eager bitwise. | AgentX c=16 | 339.97 | 303.56 | +12.0% | 307.65 | +10.5% |
| AgentX c=64 | 427.15 | 367.40 | +16.3% | 436.25 | -2.1% |

AgentX c=64 is limited by the pool at this size: Mega MoE drops from 678.66 to 427.15 tok/s. The +71% at c=64 in an earlier revision of this PR was mostly the larger pool; at equal KV it is +16%.

### Accuracy

Full GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, 128 concurrent), DP4+EP4 at KV 24 GiB, two runs on one server per arm:

| Arm | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mega MoE | 0.9378 | 0.9295 |
| main default | 0.9386 | 0.9295 |
| FI MoE-EP | 0.9363 | 0.9356 |

Paired per question, both runs pooled (A right only / B right only, exact McNemar p, paired bootstrap 95% CI):

| Pair | Discordant | p | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Mega MoE vs main default | 47 / 48 | 1.0 | -0.04 pt [-0.83, +0.80] |
| Mega MoE vs FI MoE-EP | 44 / 50 | 0.61 | -0.23 pt [-1.02, +0.61] |
| main default vs FI MoE-EP | 49 / 54 | 0.69 | -0.19 pt [-1.02, +0.64] |

Two runs of one server differ by 0.08 to 1.06 pt; the pooled gaps between arms are at most 0.23 pt. Mega MoE has no degenerate outputs. With two runs per arm, a deficit below about 1 pt cannot be ruled out. On 8x H200 at default memory: Mega MoE 0.9363 / 0.9257, main default 0.9287 / 0.9295, FI MoE-EP 0.9318 / 0.9265.

Logprobs on 320 prompts against main default (first-token top-20, 48-token greedy continuation): Mega MoE top-1 agreement 0.891, mean logprob difference 0.134, symmetric KL 0.0317, 83/320 identical continuations; FI MoE-EP 0.875, 0.140, 0.0317, 71/320. One run per arm.

Layer numerics on real weights (`Glm5NextMoE` layers 3, 15, 30, 44, 288 experts, synthetic inputs, T = 1 to 2048, relative error against float64):

| Path | Full layer rel. error | min cosine |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mega MoE (this PR) | 2.8-4.3% | 0.99910 |
| main FP8 FusedMoE, TRITON | 4.3-6.4% | 0.99870 |
| main FP8 FusedMoE, DEEPGEMM | 5.4-7.5% | 0.99799 |

Mega MoE's error equals the cost of FP8 activation quantization (within 0.001); the checkpoint's block scales reach the kernel bit exact.

### Tests

```
pytest -v -s -rs tests/models/glm5next/test_mega_moe.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py
```

H200 on main `f538463a2` with DeepGEMM `44cba7d`, after the review changes: `test_mega_moe.py` 10 passed (the scale check now reads the kernel tensor as the SM90 kernel indexes it), `test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` 109 passed and 19 skipped (SM100-only), including 6 new block-FP8 SM90 cases, `test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` 20 passed. With two broken scale layouts (no gate/up interleave, two L2 block rows swapped), the new GLM and kernel tests fail.

H200 on main `3d836e13e` with DeepGEMM `44cba7d`: `test_mega_moe.py` 10 passed, `test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` 20 passed; DeepGEMM transform test, the 14-case GLM sweep at 1 and 2 ranks and the DSv4 case pass with unchanged max calc_diff (1.62e-5). Before the rebase, H200 with DeepGEMM `b3669fe`: 123 passed, 19 skipped (all NVFP4 SM100-only; GLM and warmup tests 0 skipped). B300 on this commit with `b3669fe`: every test file gives the same result as on the PR's first commit, no failures; `test_mega_moe.py` 10 passed. Without DeepGEMM (CPU) the SM90 cases skip. DeepGEMM `b582b99` and `b3669fe` on H200, 1 and 2 ranks: transform tests, the 14-case GLM sweep, hot-expert cases, DSv4 and CUDA graph replay checks pass, max calc_diff 1.62e-5. Sanitizer, SASS and ptxas results are in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#57; they were run on `a49ea3f`, the same patch before the rebase.

## Details

**Weight format.** `MEGA_MOE_FP8_BLOCK_SM90` is `MEGA_MOE_MXFP4_SM90` with `mma_type="fp8xfp8"` and E4M3 routed and shared weights with FP32 scales per 128x128 block. A new `sm90` field on `MegaMoEWeightFormat` marks the SM90 formats; the support check and the BLOCK_M choice key on it.

**Loading.** `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` picks the SM90 format on SM90 and rejects block sizes other than 128x128. Weights load straight into the kernel layout; block scales are staged in `*_weight_scale_inv`. The kernel scales `*_weight_scale` are registered at construction in their final layout (FP32, MN-major, MN stride padded to a multiple of 4). `finalize_block_fp8_weights` lays them out with DeepGEMM's `transform_fp8_block_sf_for_sm90_mega_moe` (through a wrapper in `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`) and copies them in place, so the storage CUDA graphs captured stays valid across layerwise and direct reloads. On SM100 it calls `requantize_block_fp8` as before.

**Routing.** GLM-5.3-Flash Mega MoE routes with `fused_grouped_topk` (one group, sigmoid scoring), as Kimi K3 Mega MoE does, instead of `fused_topk_bias`, and checks at init for sigmoid scoring with a correction bias. This also applies to the SM100 FP8 and BF16 GLM Mega MoE paths. On B300 the expert ids match main's in all 32 layer cases (FP8 and BF16, padded rows included, weights within 9e-8), and decode is about 5% faster because `fused_grouped_topk` takes 2.2 µs per call against 9.6 µs. On 200k random router rows both pick the same experts (max relative weight difference 4e-7). End to end on 4x H200 (KV 24 GiB, random 1k/1k, `fused_grouped_topk` run twice), it gives +3.1% output tok/s at c=1 (mean ITL 9.16 against 9.45 ms) and +2.1% at c=16; +0.6% at c=64 and +0.3% at c=256 are within the 0.1-1.0% spread between the two runs. GSM8K shows no difference. `fused_grouped_topk` is called without the router-side padding mask, so capture hooks see real expert ids on padded rows.

**Warmup.** The DeepGEMM Mega MoE warmup now covers `Glm5NextMoE` on every GPU and weight format.

**Guards.** EPLB's expert view now accepts the padded SM90 block-scale layout, and `check_deep_gemm_mega_moe_supported` rejects SM90-only formats on SM100; neither case is reachable for GLM today. Two tests cover them.

**Docs.** The `deep_gemm_mega_moe` entry of the `moe_backend` docstring (`vllm/config/kernel.py`) now lists the supported experts per GPU: MXFP4, MXFP8, NVFP4 or BF16 on SM100, MXFP4 or 128x128 block-FP8 on SM90. The GLM-5.3-Flash recipe gets an `h200_dep_mega_moe` preset (FP8, DP + EP, opt-in) with a guide section. It is text-only for now because H200 DP with image and video input on hits an illegal memory access in encoder profiling, on main too. On 8x H200 the rendered DP8 command comes up with the default `--max-num-seqs` and scores 0.97 on the first 100 GSM8K questions; on 4x H200 it needs `--max-num-seqs 948`.

**CI.** The GLM5Next H200 job also triggers on `deep_gemm_mega_moe.py`. `test_reload_requantizes_into_the_kernel_tensors` runs SM90 × {layerwise, direct} reload. The H100 DeepGEMM Kernels job now runs `test_deep_gemm_warmup.py`, which mocks every DeepGEMM call. The SM90 cases of `test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` (#64061's MXFP4 cases and this PR's block-FP8 case) run in no CI job, because the file runs only on B200. They were run on H200.

**Not a duplicate of #62603.** #62603 (merged) added a separate opt-in backend on FlashInfer's MoE-EP CuTe DSL kernels and does not fuse the shared expert. This PR adds a weight format to the existing DeepGEMM Mega MoE backend, with the shared expert fused in the launch. Both are measured above.

**Limitations.**
- SM90 needs 128x128 block-FP8 checkpoints. BF16 GLM-5.3-Flash Mega MoE stays SM100-only.
- EP with TP=1 and one expert group, as on SM100. TP2xDP2+EP4 cannot use Mega MoE.
- `--all2all-backend` is ignored when Mega MoE is selected (as before).
- Main's default MoE backend ran out of memory at DP4+EP4 default memory, 40 s into GSM8K (FlashInfer CUTLASS asked for 4.88 GiB with 4.02 GiB free; seen once, and not at DP8+EP8). It is the failure mode of #60471 (FlashInfer CUTLASS workspace OOM after profiling; proposed fix #60570), on main and not caused by this PR.

commits.pr_title: [MM][CG] Add encoder CUDA graph support for LFM3-VL
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` support for `Lfm3VlForConditionalGeneration` (`LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B`) across image and video inputs. Related to #38175.

Because `Lfm3VlVisionModel` interleaves attention with 2D depthwise convolutions (`Lfm3VlVisionConv2d`) over variable native-resolution `(H, W)` grids, we precompute 1-based spatial neighbor indices (`conv_indices`) outside the graph and run a fused Triton gather-conv2d kernel inside the graph so arbitrary aspect ratios share one 1D token-budget graph set.

## Claims

- Image, multi-image, and video encoder CUDA Graph support for `LFM3-VL` (`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'`), leaving the default eager path (`cudagraph_mm_encoder=False`) unchanged.
- **27.3% lower Mean TTFT** (`53.02 → 38.55 ms`) and **40.7% lower P99 TTFT** (`111.10 → 65.90 ms`) on `LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B` (RTX 5070 Ti, BF16, 2 images/req @ 8 RPS).
- Exact encoder output parity on tested image budgets (`max_abs_error = 0.0`) and no accuracy degradation on MMStar (`56.67% → 57.50%`).

## Validation

### Automated tests

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k lfm3_vl -v -s
# -> 3 passed, 47 deselected in 56.27s

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/lfm3_vl.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py \
  docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md
# -> Passed
```

### E2E serving performance (`vllm bench serve`)

RTX 5070 Ti, `LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B` (`bfloat16`, TP=1, `FLASH_ATTN`), `random-mm` (2× `256x256` images + 128 text tokens, 32 output tokens, 8 RPS, 3 rounds × 200 reqs = 600 reqs/mode, budgets `[64, 128, 192, 256, 512, 1024]`):

| Metric (600 reqs/mode) | Graph Off | Graph On | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TTFT | 53.02 ms | 38.55 ms | **-27.28%** |
| Median TTFT | 48.37 ms | 36.58 ms | **-24.37%** |
| P99 TTFT | 111.10 ms | 65.90 ms | **-40.68%** |
| Graph Hits / Misses | — | 1200 / 0 | 100% hit |

<details>
<summary>Benchmark commands & per-round results</summary>

```bash
vllm serve LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":0}' \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true, "encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets": [64, 128, 192, 256, 512, 1024], "encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch": 4}'

vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B --dataset-name random-mm \
  --num-prompts 200 --request-rate 8 --seed 42 \
  --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 32 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 2 --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{(256,256,1):1.0}' \
  --temperature 0 --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,99
```

```text
Round 1 (seed=42): Off Mean 50.66 / Med 47.53 / P99 94.71 ms | On Mean 37.70 / Med 36.13 / P99 59.38 ms
Round 2 (seed=43): Off Mean 50.55 / Med 44.04 / P99 103.87 ms | On Mean 38.70 / Med 36.34 / P99 64.16 ms
Round 3 (seed=44): Off Mean 57.84 / Med 50.84 / P99 114.30 ms | On Mean 39.25 / Med 37.37 / P99 72.85 ms
```

</details>

### Quality (`Lin-Chen/MMStar`, 120 stratified samples)

| Mode | Correct | Accuracy | Graph Hits / Misses |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Graph Off | 68 / 120 | 56.67% | — |
| Graph On | 69 / 120 | 57.50% | 120 / 0 |

No accuracy degradation.

## Details

- Precomputes 1-based `conv_indices` (`0` sentinel for frame edges and tail padding) per `(H, W)` with an LRU cache, and runs a fused FP32-accumulating Triton gather-conv kernel (`_conv2d_gather_kernel`, with `_native_conv2d_gather` fallback) across `vision_tower + multi_modal_projector`.
- Falls back to eager execution (`modalities=[]`) for `TORCH_SDPA` and dynamically scaled FP8 vision attention.
- Not duplicating `#66509` (HF-vs-vLLM multimodal tests) or `#65829` (LFM3-Omni). AI assistance was used; I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Don't pin the grammar bitmask
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #67335, `allocate_token_bitmask` pins the structured-output bitmask, and #68484 removed the unpinned fallback. In EngineCore, pinning creates a CUDA context on the first structured-output request. When that fails, EngineCore dies and the server goes down with it. This PR allocates the bitmask unpinned, as the default xgrammar backend did before #67335.

## Claims

- The grammar bitmask is allocated unpinned, so the first structured-output request no longer creates a CUDA context in EngineCore.

## Validation

I hit this once on two GB10 nodes (TP=2, `mp` executor) at a87e3a6554 plus unrelated patches, with xgrammar 0.2.9 and the Rust frontend. The first `response_format` `json_schema` request killed EngineCore. The same image passed that request on two other loads. The Python frontend reaches the same EngineCore call.

<details>
<summary>EngineCore log</summary>

```
  File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 803, in step_with_batch_queue
    grammar_output = self.scheduler.get_grammar_bitmask(
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 2296, in get_grammar_bitmask
    bitmask = self.structured_output_manager.grammar_bitmask(
  File ".../vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py", line 396, in grammar_bitmask
    self._grammar_bitmask = allocate_token_bitmask(
  File ".../vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py", line 59, in allocate_token_bitmask
    return torch.full(
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory
The CUDA driver logged these messages, which may provide useful details:
Returning 2 (CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) from cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain
```

</details>

On d33bfeef40 (macOS, CPU), the new test fails on main and passes with this PR. It sets `PIN_MEMORY` and makes pinned allocation raise the error above:

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS=none HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest -q --durations=0 --durations-min=0 tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py -k does_not_pin
```

main:
```
vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py:59: in allocate_token_bitmask
E           torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory
FAILED tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py::test_allocate_token_bitmask_does_not_pin
1 failed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings in 0.13s
```

PR (4ab3601807):
```
0.00s call     tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py::test_allocate_token_bitmask_does_not_pin
1 passed, 12 deselected, 15 warnings in 0.13s
```

`tests/v1/structured_output` has the same failures on main and on this PR apart from the new test. They come from my offline Mac setup (tokenizers missing from the HF cache, no Triton). CI runs the suite in `(CPU) V1 Others`. `tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py` passes on both (66 passed). pre-commit passes.

## Details

- Root cause: the scheduler fills the bitmask on the CPU and puts `.numpy()` into `GrammarOutput`. `MultiprocExecutor` pickles it to the workers, where `StructuredOutputsWorker.apply_grammar_bitmask` copies it with `async_tensor_h2d`, which stages unpinned input through pinned memory. Pinning in EngineCore therefore saves nothing and only creates a CUDA context there. On GB10 that context creation failed in `cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain`.
- With `UniProcExecutor`, `async_tensor_h2d` now stages the used rows once per step, as it did for xgrammar before #67335 (`xgr.allocate_token_bitmask` does not pin).
- This keeps #68484's approach of not falling back: the bitmask is not pinned at all. The other caller, offline beam search, also reads the bitmask only on the CPU.
- No `LLM`-level test: CI GPUs can create the context, so the crash needs a failing context creation, which the unit test emulates.
- Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR on this (searched `allocate_token_bitmask`, pinned bitmask, structured-output CUDA OOM, follow-ups to #67335 and #68484).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix MXFP8 linear layers whose N is not a multiple of 8 or 32
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The FlashInfer MXFP8 linear kernels compute garbage or fail when a layer's N is not a multiple of 8 (CuTe-DSL) or 32 (CUTLASS). Split out of #67941, which now has only its unrelated KV cache layout fix.

## Claims

- The CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS MXFP8 linear kernels pad N with zero rows to a multiple of 8 and 32, and slice their output back to the layer's N. On `main`, CuTe-DSL wrote `inf` or garbage for such layers at M = 64, and CUTLASS raised.
- Kernel selection is unchanged, and layers with aligned N run as before.

## Validation

One node of 4x GB300 (SM103), torch 2.14, FlashInfer `main`, vLLM's compiled extensions from the wheel of `main` `26acafd`.

**The new tests** (`tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_mxfp8_unaligned_n.py`, both kernels at N = 130, 1036, 1048, 2064, 4608 and M = 1, 64, plus whichever kernel vLLM selects at N = 1036, 2072), against the dequantized reference:

- On `main`: **11 failed, 13 passed**. CUTLASS raises for every N not a multiple of 32, and CuTe-DSL is off at M = 64 for N not a multiple of 8 (M = 1 happens to come out right on its low-M split-K path):

```
RuntimeError: Check failed: n % alignment == 0 (2 vs. 0) : Expected n to be divisible by 32, but got mat2 shape: (130x256).
```

- With this PR: **24 passed**.

**Other tests that use these kernels**, run on `main` and with this PR: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py`, `test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py`, `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py`, `tests/fusion/test_quant_activation_contract.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_encoder_autotune.py` and `tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py`, `test_numerics.py`. This PR adds no failures; the same 25 fail on both (24 `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` cases, whose test layers lack `params_dtype`, and `test_specialized_decode_numerics`, which needs `ray`).

**CI:** the B200 Kernels step in `kernels.yaml` now runs `test_flashinfer_mxfp8_unaligned_n.py` and `test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py`; both skip on GPUs other than SM100.

**pre-commit** on the changed files: ruff, typos, mypy and the repo's own checks pass (the markdown, shell, GitHub Actions, C++, Rust and requirements hooks were skipped: no such files changed).

## Details

FlashInfer's CuTe-DSL MXFP8 GEMM stores its bf16/fp16 output with TMA, which needs 16-byte aligned rows (N % 8 == 0). `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel.can_implement` checks only `mm_mxfp8`'s generic limits (K ≥ 128, K % 32 == 0, N ≥ 128), so it takes such layers, and FlashInfer launched its untuned fallback tactic, which wrote garbage: at N = 130, K = 256, M = 64, a relative RMS error of 17.5 against the dequantized reference. M = 1 comes out right, so a single decode shows nothing. `FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel` needs N % 32 == 0 and neither checked nor padded it.

Both kernels now pad N in `process_weights_after_loading` with zero weight rows and scales (`_pad_n`: at most 7 or 31 extra rows per such layer, logged once per shape) and slice the GEMM output back to `output_size_per_partition`, copying it so that it stays contiguous. Layers whose N needs no padding are neither padded nor copied. The TRT-LLM kernel's existing padding to a multiple of 128 uses the same helper.

Not covered: SM120 keeps its existing N % 32 check.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Don't let later image requests overtake a request deferred for encoder limits
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #67292. With chunked prefill off and async scheduling, a multimodal request that the scheduler defers whole for encoder cache or budget limits (#65399) can be skipped indefinitely, while later requests with fewer images take the encoder cache space it needs.

With this PR, once the scheduler defers a request this way, it admits no later request that needs encoder output in that step, as long as the deferred request's images fit the configured encoder cache at once. In the issue's repro, the 4-image request is then scheduled whole at step 2, where before it was not scheduled in 50 steps.

## Claims

- Under FCFS, with chunked prefill off and async scheduling or pipeline parallelism, a request deferred for encoder limits is no longer overtaken by later requests that need encoder output, provided the embeddings of all its images add up to no more than the configured encoder cache size. It is scheduled whole once the steps in flight at the deferral have been processed, with one exception described in Details.
- In the scheduler-only repro from #67292, with `AsyncScheduler` and chunked prefill off, the 4-image request is scheduled whole at step 2. Before this change it was not scheduled in 50 steps.
- On `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` served with chunked prefill off and async scheduling under a sustained one-image load, base completed none of the 4-image requests within 30 s in any of its saturated runs, and the first version of this change completed all of them, with a median time to first token of 0.45 to 1.36 s. This includes one-image requests with `max_tokens=1`, the prefill-only and scoring case.
- Both ways the encoder step defers a request are covered. It can cut the request at the start of an image that begins after its first uncomputed token (#65399's deferral), or cut it to zero tokens because the image at its first uncomputed token does not fit.
- Later requests are not held when their tokens in the step include no image embeddings, or when the deferred request's images can't all fit the configured encoder cache at once.
- Chunked prefill on, encoder-only and encoder-decoder models, and synchronous scheduling without pipeline parallelism are unchanged.

## Validation

The unit tests ran on one H100 machine from a source tree at main (`0db6f1ba5`) with the compiled extensions of the `c02ebf136` precompiled wheel (main has no compiled-code changes since then). The CUDA runs had one GPU visible. The CPU runs had none and set `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py` passes at main's hook pins, including ruff, mypy, typos, the docstring style check and the test-tethering check.

### Tests

Four tests are added to `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, next to the test from #65399, and `create_scheduler` gains an `encoder_cache_size` argument. The tests build their scheduler with one helper, `_encoder_deferral_scheduler`, which calls `create_scheduler(model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf", max_num_batched_tokens=1024, ...)` with chunked prefill off by default. The encoder cache and budget are then 1,024 embeddings, except in the test that sets `encoder_cache_size`. CI runs this file only on the CPU platform, where `CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config` turns async scheduling off, so the helper sets the requested `async_scheduling` back on the scheduler's config after construction. State built during construction still follows the platform. The helper asserts that the async cases see overlapping batches (`max_concurrent_batches > 1`) and the sync case does not. The new tests are in a `cpu_test` file that the `pytest -v -s -m 'cpu_test' v1/core` step of the CPU CI job runs.

<details>
<summary>What each new test sets up and checks</summary>

- `test_encoder_deferred_request_is_not_overtaken` is the scenario from #67292. Three one-image requests (250 embeddings each) are in flight, a 1,020-token request arrives, and two more one-image requests arrive before every step. In the `async` case the request has 4 images (1,000 embeddings) and is cut before its second one. In the `async-cut-to-zero` case it has one 800-embedding image at token 0 and is cut to zero tokens. Both must be scheduled whole at step 2. The `sync` case (whole at step 1) and the `chunked-prefill` case (first 260 tokens at step 1) are controls that pass before and after the change.
- `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_later_requests_needing_the_encoder` checks a single step. While `deferred` waits for encoder cache space, a one-image request that would fit in the 424 free slots waits too, and a text-only request and a request whose image is in its prefix-cache hit are scheduled.
- `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_requests_with_embeddings_in_window` checks the two steps after `busy` is scheduled. Three 800-token requests each get 512 tokens from a mocked KV connector, and `tail`'s 600-token image has 400 embeddings. While `deferred` waits for 600 slots with 424 free, `tail` is scheduled when its remaining 288 tokens overlap the image only at positions without embeddings (at image offsets 0 and 40), and waits when they include embeddings. Once the first step is processed, `deferred` is scheduled in every case.
- `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_behind_requests_fitting_the_encoder_cache` sets a 600-embedding encoder cache, of which an in-flight request holds 300. A deferred request with two 300-embedding images exactly fits the cache, holds a later one-image request, and is scheduled once the in-flight step is processed. One with two 400-embedding images never fits, and the later request is scheduled.

</details>

Six cases fail with main's `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`. In the `async` and `async-cut-to-zero` cases the deferred request is not scheduled in 8 steps, which is the reported bug. In `test_encoder_deferral_holds_only_later_requests_needing_the_encoder` and the `embeds-in-window`, `embeds-in-window-offset` and `fits-cache` cases, main schedules the later request. The three cases where a later request must not be held (`no-embeds-in-window`, `no-embeds-in-window-offset` and `never-fits-cache`) fail with this PR's first commit (`fe59ae11f`), which held it. All 15 pass with the change, and the results are the same on the CPU platform (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, no GPU visible) and the CUDA platform.

On the CUDA platform it gives 3 failed and 296 passed on main, and 3 failed and 307 passed with this PR. The 3 failures are the same pipeline-parallel tests, which need two GPUs there and which CI runs on the CPU platform.

`python -m pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input` fails the same tests on main and with this PR. On CPU, 15 fail because their model configs were not available offline. On CUDA the same 15 fail, along with the 3 pipeline-parallel tests above and `test_finalize_extensible_kv_cache_auto_max_model_len_warns_when_short[True]`, which checks a warning's text and also fails on main on CUDA.

</details>

### Scheduler-only repro

The scheduler-only repro script from #67292 (`repro_overtaking_stock.py`, 50 steps, with its KV cache config updated to main's API) gives these results on `0db6f1ba5` and with this PR, on the CUDA platform.

| Scheduler | Chunked prefill | One-image requests per step | 4-image request before | 4-image request after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AsyncScheduler` | off | 1 | not scheduled in 50 steps | scheduled whole at step 2 |
| `AsyncScheduler` | off | 2 | not scheduled in 50 steps | scheduled whole at step 2 |
| `AsyncScheduler` | off | 3 | not scheduled in 50 steps | scheduled whole at step 2 |
| `Scheduler` (synchronous) | off | 2 | scheduled whole at step 1 | scheduled whole at step 1 |
| `AsyncScheduler` | on | 2 | first 300 of 1,170 tokens at step 1 | first 300 of 1,170 tokens at step 1 |

With the change, step 1 admits no image request, and at step 2 all 1,200 encoder cache slots are reclaimable when the 4-image request (1,120 embeddings) is checked. Before the change it saw 360 slots at step 1 and then 920, or 360 and 920 alternating, depending on the arrival rate.

### End to end

End to end, the starvation and the fix both reproduce on `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, served with the first version of this change applied to `3bc0f4308` on one H100. Base is `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` at `3bc0f4308`. `scheduler.py` on main has changed since that commit, and the end-to-end runs were not repeated after the rebases or the review changes. I expect the review changes not to affect them, because the runs had no prefix-cache hits, so every request was scheduled whole with all of its images' embeddings in the step, and every request's images (at most 1,120 embeddings) fit the 1,280-embedding encoder cache at once.

```text
vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18013 \
    --max-model-len 1280 --max-num-batched-tokens 1280 \
    --no-enable-chunked-prefill --async-scheduling \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "audio": 0, "video": 0}'
```

These settings make the scheduler's encoder cache and per-step encoder budget 1,280 embeddings (the engine logs `Encoder cache will be initialized with a budget of 1280 tokens`). `--max-model-len 1280` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 1280` were chosen to make the cache tight, and these runs do not measure how often the condition arises with a larger cache. Each image is a distinct 160x112 random-noise JPEG, which Gemma 4 turns into 280 embeddings, so a 4-image request (1,151 prompt tokens, 1,120 embeddings) fits only when the previous step admitted no one-image request. The load client sends one-image chat requests and, every 5 s from 5 s to 60 s of a 90 s run, a 4-image request with `max_tokens=1`, so a 4-image request's latency is its time to first token. Each 4-image request has a 30 s timeout, and the tables count a request as done only if it returned within 30 s.

<details>
<summary>The one-image requests, and how servers and image seeds were reused</summary>

The one-image chat requests have 298 or 379 prompt tokens, temperature 0, and `max_tokens=1` or `max_tokens=8` (with `max_tokens=8` they generated about 4 tokens each). Every run uses images that no other request on that server has used. Open-loop runs, the same-node pairs and the iteration-logging run each start a fresh server. In the other closed-loop jobs the 32-client run follows the 16-client run on the same server with a new image seed base, and the server log shows a 0.0% prefix cache hit rate throughout. Each configuration ran once, apart from 22 one-image requests per second and 379 tokens at 16 clients with `max_tokens=8`.

</details>

With a sustained backlog (closed loop, where each of 16 or 32 clients sends its next one-image request as soon as the previous one returns), base starves the 4-image requests and the change serves all of them. This holds when the one-image requests generate a single token, as prefill-only and scoring workloads do, and when they generate several. Across its ten saturated runs, the nine in the table and the iteration-logging run described after it, base completed none of its 120 4-image requests within 30 s. The change completed all 108 in its nine runs.

One more base run, with `--enable-logging-iteration-details` (379 tokens, `max_tokens=8`, 32 clients, 0 of 12 done), shows the mechanism. Apart from the first load steps, the steps under load alternated between admitting one new one-image request and admitting three, so the cache never had 1,120 free slots when a 4-image request was checked. With the change, a 4-image request finishes in about the time a one-image request spends queued.

<details>
<summary>Step counts from the iteration-logging run</summary>

The run logged 1,114 steps. The 12 decode-only ones fall in the warm-up and after the load ended. Of the other 1,102, one is the warm-up 4-image request, sent alone before the load. The rest admitted one new one-image request (552, one of them the warm-up request) or three (549), alternating apart from the first load steps.
